description:
Moderate sized, solitary or clustering, monoecious palms. Stem often with green internodes, distinct leaf scars distally, and a cone of adventitious roots basally. Leaves 5–10 in crown, spirally arranged; sheath tubular forming a yellowish to brownish tinged green crownshaft; petiole very short or less than 50 cm long, unarmed, smooth; blade splitting in usually regularly distributed, one to several folded, narrowly sigmoid pinnae, distributed in one plane, leaf apex often composed of several irregularly splitting, closely inserted pinnae. Inflorescence infrafoliar, branched from first to third order, sheathed in bud only by the prophyll, this thinly coriaceous and early deciduous, peduncle short, inflorescence branches spreading to stiffly erect. Unisexual flowers in cymose flower cluster of two to three, or solitary towards the rachillae apices, female flowers much larger than male flowers, only fully developed at the very base of the rachillae, male flowering part of rachillae wilting and often present as tails in the infructescence. Fruit one seeded, epicarp smooth usually red at maturity, mesocarp usually thin, fleshy to fibrous, endocarp composed of longitudinal fibres, more or less free at the base, endosperm deeply ruminate.

Fifty species found in tropical and subtropical Asia; four species native in Thailand, one (A. catechu) is only known from cultivation and not included here since it has not been recorded from the wild (Plate XCVIII: A).

description: Solitary or clustering palm tree up to 4 m tall. Stem c. 1.5–2.5 cm diam. Leaf: petioleshort, c. 10 cm long or less; rachis short probably not more than 1 m long, with few irregularly spaced pinnae. Inflorescence branched to second order with more than 15, spirally arranged, yellowish-green, first order branches. Male flowers mostly inserted in pairs, with 6 stamens. Fruit rather large to 3.5 cm long.

description: Solitary palm, with individual stems up to 6 m tall and 7 cm diam. Leaves 5–8 in crown; leaf sheath forming a yellowish-green up to 50 cm long crownshaft; petiole 20–40 cm long, green glabrous; rachis 0.8–1.3 m long, with 5–15 pinnae per side, longest ones in the middle, 40–60 cm long. Inflorescence branched to three orders, peduncle 1–3 cm long, rachis 10–25 cm long, flowering branches yellowish-green, rachillae 10–15 cm long, male flowers mostly paired, with 3 stamens. Fruit ellipsoid to ovoid, 2–3 by 1–1.5 cm, red.

description: Solitary palm, up to 5 m tall and 5 cm diam. Leaves 8–12 in crown; leaf sheath forming a brownish-green up to 45 cm long crownshaft; petiole 15–20 cm long, green glabrous; rachis up to 2.5 m long, with 5–15 or rarely more pinnae on each side, longest pinnae in the middle, up to 70 cm long. Inflorescence branched to first order (rarely to second), peduncle 2–3 cm long, rachis 10–15 cm, flowering branches up to 15, distichously arranged, stiffl y upright, dark purplish to brown, 15–30 cm long. Male flowers paired or solitary, with 6 stamens. Fruit ellipsoid to ovoid, 3–4.5 by 1.5–3 cm, purplish-green to brown.

description: Low shrubs to robust tree palms, solitary or clustered, monoecious usually with unisexual inflorescences, male and female flowering separated in time, pleonanthic or hapaxanthic. Leaves imparipinnate, induplicate; leaf sheath usually disintegrating into a fibrous mesh; petiole slender to very robust; leafl ets regularly arranged in one plane or unevenly arranged in several planes, strongly asymmetrical at the base, sometimes with one or two auricles. Flowering acropetal in pleonanthic species, basipetal in hapaxanthic species. Inflorescence enclosed in numerous bracts, branched to first or second order, drooping, unisexual, in hapaxanthic species the female ones produced distally before the male ones. Flowers dimorphic. Male flowers usually with more than 15 functional stamens, and without a pistillode. Female flowers with globose ovary, sessile stigmas and 2–3 locules. Fruit globose to ellipsoidal, often somewhat angled, 1–3 seeded; epicarp smooth, dull to brightly coloured, mesocarp fleshy, with high density of raphide-containing ideoblasts causing skin irritation, endocarp not differentiated. Seed with homogeneous endosperm.</br></br>Twenty four species with three varieties in tropical and subtropical Asia to N Australia. Five species in Thailand.

description: Densely clustered shrub. Stem 0.6–2 cm diam. Leaves c. 10 in crown; sheath deeply split, with margins resolving in fibrous mesh, petiole 30–60 cm long; rachis to 60 cm long; lamina divided into 4–10 rhomboid to linear pinnae on each side, 20–80 by 2–10 cm, dark green, distinctly silvery grey below, apical margins praemorse. Inflorescences 2–3, interfoliar, developing in basipetal sequence, the most distal one usually female, the others male, spicate, or rarely with secondary branches, 25–30 cm long, curved. Fruit 1–1.5 cm diam., globose, orange to red, densely inserted.

description: Loosely clustered tree, to 15 m tall, pleonanthic. Stem 20–30 cm diam., internodes grey, ringed by leaf scars. Leaves 12–15 in crown, pinnate; sheath 60–100 cm long, deeply split, persietent grey, distintegrating along the margins in mesh of coarse, black fibres; petiole 30-90 cm long; rachis 4–8(–10) m long, curved distally; pinnae 100–105 on each side of rachis, 100–150 by 6–9 cm, lanceolate, evenly distributed, in one plane or slightly plumose, silvery grey below, with praemorse margins. Inflorescence 2-4, interfoliar, flowering sequence on stem acropetal; peduncle 20–75 cm long, c. 6 cm wide, upright and curved; rachis 30–75 cm long, drooping; rachillae 20–60 to 25–45 cm long, drooping. Fruit 4–6 by 3–4 cm, oblong, subtriangular in cross section, light green when young to yellowish-green at maturity. Seed elongate, keeled, basally with white scar from the funicle.

description: Solitary palm tree to 20 m tall, hapaxanthic. Stem 40–60 cm diam., usually covered to the base by persistent leaf sheaths, basally with a cone of adventitious roots. Leaves 12–15 in crown; sheaths deeply split, 80–90 cm long, disintegrating along the margins into a mesh of coarse, black fibres; petiole 100–130 cm long, rachis 4–8 m long, pinnae 80–150 on each side, 100–130 by 6–10 cm, evenly distributed in one plane, only rarely pointing in different directions, silvery grey with rusty tinge below, praemorse distally, terminal pair often united and wider. Inflorescences 4–6, interfoliar, flowering sequence on stem basipetal; peduncle 30–60 cm long, upright, and curved; rachis 0.8–1.2 m long, drooping; rachillae 40–70, to 0.6–1.6 m long, drooping. Fruit globose or slightly longer than wide, 5–7 cm diam., bluish-green or dark green at maturity. Seed elongate to elliptic, with a sharp keel, scar from funicle inconspicuous.

description: Solitary, dioecious, pleonanthic palm trees. Leaves induplicate, costapalmate; leaf sheath splitting to the base, fibrous along margins, with additional triangular cleft below the petiole; petiole robust, deeply channelled above, margins smooth and very sharp; adaxial hastula well developed, abaxial hastula reduced or absent, blade deeply divided into several folded segments, these further parted into single-folded segments, transverse veinlets conspicuous. Inflorescences interfoliar, dimorphic, enclosed at the base in the prophyll and one to few peduncular bracts, more or less drooping at anthesis. Male inflorescences branched to second order, male rachillae with tight spiral of imbricate bracts, subtending and covering sympodial flower clusters of 2–6 flowers, male flowers exserted one at a time as they pass into anthesis, stamens 6–15, pistillode minute to absent. Female inflorescence spicate or with few branches, with tight spiral of overlapping bracts, each subtending a single female flower, this much larger than male flower and only partly covered by the bracts, staminodes much reduced, gynoecium globose, 3-loculate with sessile stigmas. Fruit large, rounded, usually 3-seeded, rarely with fewer seeds, epicarp smooth, mesocarp fibrous, endocarp around individual pyrenes very thick and grooved. Seed with homogeneous endosperm.</br></br>Two species, Peninsular Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo. One species in Thailand.

description: Massive, solitary tree palm, up to 20 m tall. Stem 20–30 cm diam. Leaves 40–45 in crown; petiole 3–4 m long; costa 80–100 cm long; lamina 3–3.5 m across; deeply divided into 70–80 segments, these 140–170 cm long, dark green on both surfaces, and further divided to about the middle in more or less drooping, one folded segments, giving an overall untidy appearance to the leaf. Inflorescences up to 8 on one palm, drooping; male inflorescence with 20–40 cm long peduncle, rachis 1–1.5 m long with 5–9 first order branches each bearing 3–4 rachillae clustered towards the apex; rachillae 30–40 cm long, 4–6 cm diam., male flowers 1.7–2 cm long at anthesis; female inflorescence with 30–50 cm long peduncle, rachis 40–60 cm long, unbranched or with up to 3 flower bearing branches; female flowers 2.8–3.2 cm long at anthesis. Fruit obovoid, 8–16 by 7–13 cm, yellowish-black at maturity.

description: Solitary, dioecious, pleonanthic palm trees. Leaves induplicate, costapalmate; leaf sheath splitting to the base, fibrous along margins, with additional triangular cleft below the petiole; petiole robust, flattened adaxially, margins armed with short spines, irregular in size and shape; adaxial hastula well developed, abaxial hastula a low ridge; blade divided approximately halfway to the middle in stiff, bifid, single-folded segments, transverse veinlets conspicuous. Inflorescence interfoliar, dimorphic, enclosed at the base by the prophyll, peduncular bracts lacking or highly reduced. Male inflorescences branched to second order, male rachillae with tight spiral of imbricate bracts, subtending and covering sympodial flower clusters of 4–7 flowers, exserted one at a time as they pass into anthesis, stamens 6, pistillode minute. Female inflorescence spicate or with few branches, with tight spiral of overlapping bracts, each subtending a single pistillate flower, this much larger than male flower and only partly covered by the bracts, staminodes much reduced, gynoecium globose, three-loculate with sessile stigmas. Fruit large, rounded, usually 3-seeded, rarely less, epicarp smooth, mesocarp fibrous, endocarp around individual pyrenes hard and bony. Seed with homogeneous endosperm.</br></br>Five species in NE Tropical Africa, Madagascar, Tropical Asia, Malesia. One species in Thailand, possibly native, but widely cultivated.

description: Solitary tree palm, up to 20 m tall. Stem grey and clean or sometimes covered to the base by persistent leaf bases, 25–30 cm diam. Leaves 40–50 in crown, lower ones marcescent; petiole 1.5–2 m long; costa 0.6–1.1 m long; lamina 1.2–1.8 m across, undulate and untidy looking, parted about halfway in 60–65 stiff, single-folded segments, green on both surfaces. Male inflorescence with 50–60 cm long peduncle, rachis 40–50 cm long with 5–7 first order branches each bearing 2–3, 35–50 cm long rachillae; male flowers 0.5–0.7 cm long at anthesis; female inflorescence with 40–50 cm long peduncle, rachis 20–85 cm long, unbranched, rarely with a few additional flower bearing branches; female flowers 2.8–3.2 cm long at anthesis. Fruit obovoid, 10–12 by 8–10 cm, leaden blue to black at maturity.

description: Solitary or clustering, stemless to high-climbing or erect pleonanthic dioecious rattans; sheaths usually heavily armed with spines, the spines frequently highly organized; flagellum (sterile inflorescence) often present, borne on the leaf sheath, sometimes absent and replaced by a cirrus at the end of the leaf, very rarely both present or both absent; knee often present; ocrea sometimes well developed, usually inconspicuous. Male and female inflorescences superficially similar, often ending in a long flagellum, sometimes with gradual succession of branches, often with discrete distant branches (partial inflorescences); bracts always tubular at the base, rarely with broad limbs splitting down one side but, if so, then the base always tubular and unsplit, bracts variously armed; partial inflorescences usually much longer than the subtending bract, very rarely shorter, floral bracteoles inconspicuous. Male flower solitary in each rachilla bract, with cup-shaped calyx, usually with 3 well defined lobes; corolla split almost to the base into 3 petals; stamens 6 (very rarely 12), very shortly epipetalous; pistillode minute. Female flower borne together with a sterile male flower as a pair; sterile male flower like the fertile male, but with empty anthers; female flower usually larger than the male, with calyx shallowly 3-lobed; corolla with 3 petals; staminodes 6, joined basally to form a ring; ovary tipped with 3 stigmas and covered with reflexed scales; locules 3 with one ovule in each. Fruit variously shaped, covered in reflexed scales. Seed usually one only, rarely 3 developing, very variable in shape, covered in a thin to thick sarcotesta; endosperm homogeneous or ruminate; embryo basal or lateral. Seedling leaf bifid or pinnate.</br></br>About 388 species: Africa, Sri Lanka, India and South China, southwards through Malesia to Australia and Fiji. Reaches its greatest diversity in Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo with a secondary centre of diversity in New Guinea. Fifty four species with two subspecies and four varieties in Thailand.</br></br>Calamus can only be identified to genus by a combination of characters. Together with Ceratolobus, Daemonorops and Pogonotium it forms a group of closely related genera in which the female inflorescence bears dyads – pairs of flowers, each consisting of a female flower together with a sterile male flower – while the male inflorescence bears male flowers singly. The differences between these genera are based mostly on the overall structure of the inflorescence, in particular the nature of the bracts. The most reliable character separating Calamus is the persistent tubular nature of the bracts. Some generalisations can be made – rattans with flagella must belong to Calamus, though not all species of Calamus bear flagella. Rattans with subcirrate leaves are usually species of Calamus. If the endosperm is homogeneous, then the rattan cannot belong to Daemonorops, but ruminate endosperms are found in both genera. The differences are summarized in the key to genera. With practice the genera are eventually easily distinguished.

description: Dwarf acaulescent rattan. Stem very short, bulbous, erect, usually mostly subterranean, up to c. 5 cm diam. Leaves ecirrate, to 1.5 m long; leaf bases thick, leathery, surrounding the bulbous stem; knee absent; flagellum absent; petiole up to 90 cm long, the sheathing base split open, tubular only in the young state, distally petiole c. 0.5 cm wide, sparsely armed with yellow spines to 0.5 cm long; leaflets to 14 on each side of the rachis, arranged in groups of 2–3, held in different planes, the whole leaf hence plumose, longest leaflets 15–23 by 0.8–1.5 cm, armed with abundant stiff yellow spines on adaxial surface of the midrib and along margins. Inflorescences erect, 0.4–1.1 m long, male and female superficially similar, the male branching to 1 or 2 orders, the female to 1 order. Fruit c. 1.2 by 0.9 cm, ± rounded, with a short beak to 0.2 cm, and covered in 13–14 vertical rows of ivory-coloured scales with dark margins. Seed c. 0.7 by 0.6 by 0.4 cm; endosperm homogeneous.

description: Solitary or sparsely clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 30 m or more long, without sheaths c. 0.9 cm diam., with sheaths 1.5–2.5 cm diam., internodes 20–30 cm long. Leaf ecirrate; sheath dark green with scattered pale brown indumentum and abundant fragile spines, mostly slender, needle-like, 0.5–1 cm long, scattered in between larger bulbous based spines to 1.2 cm long; knee conspicuous, more sparsely armed than the rest of the sheath; ocrea short, to 1 cm long, covered in abundant dark spines to 0.3 cm long; flagellum to 1.5 m long; petiole short, to 3 cm long; rachis to 1 m long, bearing 9–10, regularly arranged, broad lanceolate, acuminate, concolorous, dark green leaflets, bearing abundant bristles along margins and on upper surface of veins. Inflorescences rather stiff, 0.7–1.4 m long, rather distant partial inflorescences, male and female superficially similar, male branching to 3 orders, the female to 2, with c. 5 rather distant, evenly spaced partial inflorescences with recurved axes; male rachillae 6–7 by 0.2 cm; female rachillae 5–7 by 0.3 cm, with very conspicuous flower cluster scars. Mature fruit ovoid, c. 2.4 by 1.5 cm, shortly beaked, covered in 13 vertical rows of yellowish-green scales with reddish margins, drying dark brown. Seed ovoid c. 1.8 by 1 cm; endosperm ruminate.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Moderate to robust clustering erect rattan showing no tendency to climb. Stems to 10 m long, 6.5 cm diam., internodes short, to 10 cm long. Leaf ecirrate; sheaths green, open and tubular only at the base, armed densely with scattered or partially whorled flattened black spines, to 4 cm long; ocrea present; knee absent; flagellum absent; petiole 0.5–1.5 m long, densely armed with flattened black spines to 8 cm long, arranged in partial whorls; rachis to 2.5–4 m long; leaflets 25–90 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, ± lanceolate, adaxially dark green, abaxially with a dense layer of whitish indumentum, the largest to 1 by 0.06 m. Inflorescences to 2.5 m long, without terminal flagellum, male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; primary bracts splitting and tattering at their tips; partial inflorescences up to 15, to 60 cm long; male rachillae 12–19 by 0.3 cm, female to 18 by 0.4 cm. Fruits obovoid to ellipsoid, to 2.2 by 0.5 cm, shortly beaked and covered in 12 vertical rows of reddish-brown deeply channelled scales. Seed 1.2 by 0.6 cm, irregularly pitted; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf not recorded.

description: Clustering moderate high-climbing rattan. Stems to 40 m or more long, without sheaths to 1.3 cm diam., with sheaths to 2.5 cm diam., internodes to 15 cm long at maturity, longer in juvenile stems. Leaf cirrate; sheaths dull green, armed with scattered, green, basally pale, black-tipped spines to 2.5 by 0.5 cm, with much smaller spines scattered in between; knee conspicuous; ocrea dark brown, tattering, to 0.6 cm high; leaf to 2 m long including the cirrus to 75 cm; petiole either absent or rather short, sparsely armed, channelled on the upper surface; leaflets c. 20 on each side of the rachis, subregularly arranged near the base, in pairs distally or in pairs throughout, the longest to c. 45 by 4 cm, sometimes much shorter and broader, very slightly bristly at the tip, concolorous. Male and female inflorescences superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to two orders, 0.8–1.2 m long, with c. 6 partial inflorescences to 15 cm long; rachillae reflexed, male to 2.5 cm long, the female to c. 6 cm long. Mature fruit ovoid, c. 1.1 by 0.9 cm, shortly beaked, covered in up to 26 rows of dull straw-coloured overlapping scales. Seed to 0.8 by 0.5 by 0.4 cm; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf not recorded.

description: Solitary or clustering moderate rattan. Stem climbing to 15 m or more, without sheaths c. 1 cm diam., with sheaths to c. 2 cm diam., internodes to c. 10 cm long. Leaf ecirrate; sheaths rather densely armed with dark brown spines of varying length, reflexed or patent, the longest to 5 cm long, 0.5 cm wide at the base, spines around the leaf sheath mouth erect, to 10 cm long, brown indumentum abundant between spines; knee conspicuous; ocrea inconspicuous; flagellum to 2 m long; petiole to 15 cm long; rachis to 1.85 m long, it and the petiole rather densely covered with pale to mid-brown indumentum and scattered spines, particularly along margins; leaflets to c. 50–90 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, close, linear, the largest to 28 by 1.6 cm, adaxially with 3 veins, bristly, abaxially very densely armed with minute bristles. Inflorescences flagellate, male and female superficially similar, to c. 3.5 m long, with 5–9 partial inflorescences, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2; male rachillae c. 1.5 by 0.3 cm; female rachillae to 7.5 by 0.15 cm. Mature fruit unknown; immature fruit green with 22 vertical rows of scales.

description: Slender clustering rattan. Stem climbing to 20 m, without sheaths 0.6–0.8 cm diam., with sheaths 1–1.2 cm diam., internodes 5–12 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; leaf sheath rather densely covered with solitary spines 0.1–1.3 cm long, with slightly swollen bases, thin scattered pale brown tomentum present between the spines; knee prominent, c. 0.3 cm high, unarmed or more sparsely armed than the sheath; flagellum to 125 cm long; petiole 7–12.5 cm long, c. 0.4 cm wide, armed abaxially and laterally with recurved spines to 0.4 cm, adaxially ± unarmed; rachis 22–47 cm long, armed abaxially with recurved spines; leaflets rhomboid, 5–6 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged but rather distant, apical pair divergent, basal leaflets 6–10 by 2.8–4.6 cm, middle leaflets 9–17.5 by 3.5–6.5 cm, with numerous radiating veins, transverse veinlets conspicuous, margins undulate and bearing sparse black bristles. Inflorescence (only female known) to 90 cm long including terminal flagellum to 60 cm long, branching to 2 orders, with 1–3 partial inflorescences; prophyll strictly tubular, entire, 8–19 cm long, armed with scattered reflexed spines, rachis bracts similar; partial inflorescences inserted on the rachis at the mouth of the subtending bract; rachillae 5–7, distichously arranged, 1–4 cm long, c. 0.15–0.2 cm diam., ± straight, appearing zig-zag from flower insertions; rachilla bracts striate. Female flower c. 0.3 by 0.2 cm. Fruit broadly ovoid, abruptly beaked, beak to 1.8 by 1.4 cm; scales straw yellow with dark margins, arranged in 18 vertical rows. Seed c. 1 by 0.7–0.8 cm, coarsely pitted; endosperm ruminate. Seedling leaf with two divergent rhomboid leaflets.

description: Differing from the typical variety in being generally much shorter, often flowering at ground level, in having inflorescence rachis bracts conspicuously tattered and split to the base, the partial inflorescences inserted just above the bract insertion, and the narrow ellipsoid fruit with scales in 20 vertical rows. Known from incomplete material – male inflorescence branching to 3 orders, female to 2 orders.

description: Clustering moderate-sized rattan forming thickets. Stems climbing to 20 m or more, without sheaths 1.5 cm diam., with sheaths to 3.5 cm diam., internodes to c. 20 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths dull green, armed with scattered triangular green, black-tipped spines to 1.2 by 0.4 cm, with swollen yellowish bases, the spines solitary or grouped in twos or threes, pale brown indumentum abundant between the spines; knee conspicuous; ocrea to 0.5 cm high, densely hispid; flagellum to 4 m long; petiole to c. 40 cm long, sparsely armed wth spines; rachis to 1.1 m long; leaflets c. 40 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, rather close, linear to narrow lanceolate, arcuate, the longest to 35 by 2 cm, rather abruptly decreasing to 10 by 1.5 cm near the leaf tip, drying pale green, apical pair joined basally, leaflets armed with bristles on 3 veins adaxially, sometimes on the mid vein abaxially. Inflorescences flagellate, to 4 m long, bearing 7 or more distant partial inflorescences, the male branched to 3 orders the female to 2 orders; male rachillae very short bearing congested flowers; female rachillae arcuate, neartly distichous and rather distant, to 10 cm long. Mature fruit ellipsoid, 1–1.2 by 0.5–0.6 cm, very shortly beaked, covered in 15–16 vertical rows of pale green or whitish scales with dark margins. Seed 0.8–0.9 by 0.3–0.4 cm, oblong to pointed at both ends, shallowly pitted, sarcotesta green, extremely sour and bitter; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf with 4 very fine small divaricate leaflets.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Clustering, moderate-sized rattan. Stems potentially climbing to great heights, to 100 m or more, usually much less due to over-exploitation, the clump tending to be very close and dense, without sheaths 0.7–1.8 cm diam., with sheaths to 2.5 cm diam., internodes to 50 cm long, sometimes even longer in juveniles, bare stem highly polished, covered with a shiny silica layer, breaking off in flakes when stem bent. Leaves cirrate; sheaths dull green, armed with sparse pale triangular spines to 1.5 by 0.5 cm; knee prominent; petiole present in juveniles, absent in adult stem; rachis to 75 cm long; cirrus to 75 cm long; leaflets c. 15 on each side of the rachis, irregularly arranged, usually in alternate pairs, dark green adaxially, abaxially covered in dense grey-white indumentum, the leaflets thus conspicuously discolorous somewhat plicate and cucullate, the longest to 30 by 5 cm. Inflorescence to 2 m long, with 7 or more partial inflorescence; bracts strictly tubular with sparse brown indumentum; male rachillae up to 3 cm long, female rachillae to 10 cm long. Ripe fruit ovoid, c. 1.5 by 1 cm, with a beak to 0.2 by 0.2 cm, and covered in 15–21 vertical rows of greenish-white scales, drying pale straw coloured. Seed ovoid, c. 1.2 by 0.7 cm; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf forked, the two lobes parallel, ¼ the length of the whole lamina, adaxially dark green, abaxially greyish-white.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus caesius . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 353. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Clustering acaulescent non-climbing palm of the forest undergrowth. Stem usually completely subterranean or shortly erect or prostrate, to 1.5 m long, without sheaths to 8 cm diam., with sheaths to 12 cm diam., internodes very short, rarely exceeding 3 cm long. Leaf ecirrate to 4 m long; sheaths tubular within the bud but soon splitting and becoming open, dull green, armed with flattened grey, yellow-based grouped spines variable in length, 0.2–8 cm; tattered bristly ligule present on the margins of the sheath mouth; flagellum absent; petiole up to 2.5 m long, distally rounded in cross section, armed as the sheath; rachis to 5 m long; leaflets c. 30–40 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, linear-lanceolate, the largest to 50 by 3 cm, shining dark green adaxially, abaxially covered with a layer of dirty-grey indumentum, armed with 3 rows of black bristles abaxially and sometimes on main vein adaxially. Inflorescences to 45 cm long, borne low down on the leaf sheaths, their bases usually obscured by spines and debris, male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; male rachillae to 4 cm long, c. 0.4 cm diam., bearing distichous bracts, pinkish or crimson when newly emerged; female rachillae fewer and longer, to 12 cm long, 0.5 cm diam., bracts similarly coloured to the male. Mature fruit ellipsoid, to 2.5 by 1.8 cm, strongly beaked, covered in 18–27 vertical rows of chestnut brown scales. Seed c. 1.8 by 1.2 cm; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf with 6 leaflets, dark green adaxially, abaxially covered with grey indumentum.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus castaneus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 354. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Very short clustering rattan. Stems erect or procumbent, not climbing, to 4–5 m long, without sheaths 3.5–5 cm diam., with sheaths to 8 cm diam., internodes short, rarely exceeding 8 cm long, usually less. Leaves ecirrate; sheath open through much of its length, densely armed with large flattened straw-coloured triangular spines to 4 cm long, 1 cm wide at the swollen green bases, the spines solitary or grouped into partial whorls, pale to mid-brown indumentum abundant between the spines; ocrea conspicuous, to 75 cm long, soon tattering, densely bristly; knee absent; flagellum absent; petiole up to 1.5 m or more long, armed as the sheath; rachis to 3.5 m long; leaflets 35–60 on each side of the rachis, irregularly arranged, in groups of 2–5, slightly fanned within the groups, sometimes almost regular, linear lanceolate, the longest to 70 by 5 cm, drying pale dull green, armed with pale bristles on margins and adaxially on the main vein and abaxially along three veins. Inflorescences male and female superficially similar, erect or arching, to 2 m long, not flagellate, bearing 4–10 partial inflorescences, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; rachis bracts rather inflated, loosely tubular, armed with scattered spines; male rachillae very crowded to 2.5 by 0.3 cm; female rachillae to 10 by 0.5 cm. Fruit rounded, conspicuously beaked, c. 0.8 cm diam., covered in 15–18 vertical rows of straw-coloured scales. Seed c. 0.5 cm diam., slightly furrowed; endosperm homogeneous.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Clustering high climbing moderate-sized rattan. Stems to 40 m long, without sheaths 2.2 cm diam., with sheaths to 4 cm diam.; internodes to 30 cm long. Leaf ecirrate; sheaths bright to yellowish-green, very densely armed with reflexed triangular blackish spines with pale bases, the spines very variable, the longest to 2.2 by 1 cm, sometimes with hairy margins, the spine bases sometimes joined by swollen ridges, caducous black indumentum abundant between the spines; knee conspicuous; ocrea inconspicuous; flagellum to 3 m long; petiole to 20 cm in juvenile shoots, usually ± absent in adult leaves; rachis arcuate to 2 m long, armed with short reflexed spines; leaflets linear, up to c. 60 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, the longest to c. 30 by 1.5 cm, conspicuously bristly along margins, and 3 veins adaxially and the main vein abaxially. Inflorescences flagellate, 3–5 m long, the male and female superficially similar, bearing up to 6 rather distant partial inflorescences, the male inflorescence branched to 3 orders the female to 2 orders; male rachillae crowded, to 3–4 by 0.2 cm, the female lax, to 10 by 0.4 cm. Mature fruit ovoid, to 2 by 1.2 cm, strongly beaked, covered in 18 vertical rows of straw-coloured scales. Seed c. 1.2 by 0.9 cm, somewhat angular, pitted; endosperm ruminate.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus densiflorus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 355. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 20 m or more, without sheaths to c. 1.5 cm diam., with sheaths to 3 cm diam., internodes to c. 15 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths dull, often brownish-green, drying brown, armed with long black flattened spines to 4 cm long, usually less, sometimes with conspicuous swollen bases, brown scales abundant between the spines; knee conspicuous; ocrea poorly developed; flagellum to 2 m long; petiole 20–40 cm long; rachis curved, to 1 m long; leaflets c. 15–30 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, curved, linear, the longest (in one form) to 35 by 1.4 cm, or (in another form) to 50 by 2 cm, bristly on main vein on upper surface, armed with 3 rows of bristles or densely covered with bristles on the lower surface. Inflorescence to 4 m, the male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, with c. 5 very distant, partial inflorescences, long pendulous; male rachillae c. 5 by 0.2 cm; female rachillae c. 7 by 0.3 cm. Mature fruit rounded, c. 2.2 cm diam., shortly beaked and covered in 16–21 vertical rows of brown scales. Seed rounded, 1–1.2 cm diam., deeply pitted; endosperm ruminate. Seedling leaf bifid.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus diepenhorstii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 356. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Clustering massive erect non-climbing rattan. Stems to 6 m tall, without sheaths 3–5 cm diam., with sheaths to 7 cm diam., internodes short, not usually exceeding 8 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths open, tubular only when very young, light to dark green, armed with partial whorls of flattened black spines 2–5 cm long, interspersed with black needle-like spicules and dark brown indumentum; knee absent; ocrea to over 15 cm long, covered in short black bristles, and splitting into two, forming auricles on either side of the petiole, auricles eventually disintegrating; flagellum absent; petioles of upper leaves 50–150 cm long, much longer in rosette leaves, rounded in cross section, armed with whorls of long, straw-coloured spines to 5–15 cm long; rachis to 350 cm, armed as the petiole; leaflets c. 40 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged except in juvenile leaves where somewhat irregular, the longest 60–80 by 3.5–5 cm, mid vein with short or long bristles on both surfaces and along margins. Inflorescence lacking a terminal flagellum and with numerous rather crowded partial inflorescences; male and female inflorescences superficially similar, erect, to 2 m long, the male branching to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; primary bracts tubular but becoming lacerated at the tips; male rachillae to 10–20 by 0.3 cm, female to 11 by 0.3 cm. Fruits ellipsoid, 3–5 by 2–2.5 cm with a short beak to 0.2 by 0.2 cm, and covered with 14–15 vertical rows of reddish-brown deeply grooved scales with dark and light patches. Seed 2–3.5 by 1.2–2.9 cm, endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf not recorded.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus erectus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 357. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Robust clustering rattan tending to form thickets on the landward side of mangrove or behind coastal sand bars. Stem climbing to 15 m, without sheaths 2–3.5 cm diam., with sheaths to 5 cm diam., rarely more, internodes to c. 30 cm. Leaves cirrate; sheaths orangish-yellow to yellowish-green when fresh, very densely armed with slender greyish-brown spines, 0.2–3.5 cm long, held horizontally and arranged in horizontal or oblique whorls, spines and sheath epidermis densely covered with grey deciduous indumentum; spines around the leaf sheath mouth upward-pointing, in groups of 5–9, the longest to 6 cm; knee and base of petiole very conspicuous, unarmed, orange-yellow, when young densely covered with indumentum; petiole to 25 cm long, armed along the margins only with grouped spines to 3 cm long; rachis to 2.25 m long; cirrus to 2 m; leaflets to 70 or more on each side of the rachis, greyish-green, very regular, close, limply pendulous, the longest to 40 by 2 cm, armed with short bristles along the margins and on the veins on the lower surface, the lower surface also with white wax and minute brown scales. Inflorescences to 1.5 m long, male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, with very short peduncle enclosed by the leaf sheath; primary bracts armed with groups of short spines; partial inflorescences about 7 on each side of the axis, gradually decreasing in size distally; male rachillae 1–2 cm long with close distichous flowers; female rachillae 10 cm long with laxer distichous flowers. Fruit rounded, to 1 cm diam., covered in 12 vertical rows of straw-coloured scales. Seed rounded, c. 0.7 cm diam.; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf not recorded.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus erinaceus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 357. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Slender solitary or clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 15 m long, usually less, without sheaths 0.4–0.6 cm diam., with sheaths 1.5 cm (rarely to 2.5 cm) diam.; internodes to 15 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths dull greyish-brown, vary variable in armature, always very densely covered with minute spines giving a scabrid feel to the whole sheath, triangular spines to 1.2 cm long with hairy margins sometimes also present on the sheaths, particularly in montane populations; knee conspicuous, armed as the sheath; ocrea inconspicuous; flagellum to 1.75 m long; petiole to 15 cm long; rachis 20–40 cm long, scabrid as the leaf sheaths, bearing conspicuous pale chestnut-brown hairs adaxially among the bases of the leaflets; leaflets 20–25 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, to 15 by 0.8 cm, rather thin in texture, densely covered with fine pale bristles on both surfaces and margins, rarely these bristles almost absent. Inflorescences flagellate, to 75 cm long, with 2–7 partial inflorescences, the male inflorescence branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; rachillae of both sexes strongly reflexed, the male to 1 by 0.1 cm, the female to 4 by 0.3 cm, the flower groups with conspicuous circular cup-like attachment. Mature fruit ovoid to oblong, to 1.3 by 0.8 cm, borne on a large disk, shortly beaked, covered in 15–18 vertical rows of straw-coloured scales. Seed ovoid to oblong, c. 1 by 0.6 cm, flattened on one side, very deeply and sinuously grooved, the whole with a thin, green, intensely bitter and foetid sarcotesta; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf pinnate with up to 10 ciliate hairy leafl ets on each side and conspicuous rusty hairs adaxially along the rachis.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus exilis . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 358. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Robust clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 30 m or more long, without sheaths 1.5–3 cm diam., with sheaths 3.5–5 cm diam.; internodes to 30 cm. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths generally not splitting opposite the petiole, greenish-yellow with reddish-brown indumentum and very densely armed with a variety of different spine types, large flattened straw coloured spines to 6 cm long, with paler swollen bases tending to be arranged in groups, and abundant small black spicules to 0.5 cm long scattered or in groups, spines around the leaf sheath mouth ± erect, to 10 cm long; ocrea to 15 cm long, covered in black spicules, split to form two auricles on each side of the petiole, soon splitting further, tattering and disintegrating; knee present but rather poorly developed and partially obscured by spines; flagellum massive, to 6 m long; petiole 30–70 cm long, armed as the leaf sheath but more sparsely; leaf rachis to 2 m long; leaflets to 35 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, rather distant, lanceolate, the largest 60–70 by 3.5–4.5 cm, conspicuous black bristles present along the main vein on both surfaces and along margins. Inflorescences male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, with 6 or more very distant pendulous partial inflorescences, to 60 cm long; male rachillae 9 by 0.25 cm; female rachillae to 13 by 0.4 cm. Mature fruit ovoid, 2.5–3 by 1.1–1.8 cm, covered with 12–13 vertical rows of channelled scales; seed ovoid, c. 2 by 1.4 cm; endosperm ruminate.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus flagellum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 359. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Slender clustering rattan. All parts drying pale green. Stem without sheaths c. 0.9 cm diam., with sheaths c. 1.5 cm diam., internodes 15–17 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths bearing scattered triangular, somewhat flattened black spines to 1.1 by 0.6 cm, with paler bases, the spine bases sometimes rather oblique and downswept, these often interspersed with much smaller black spines to 0.2 cm long, also with swollen bases, scattered caducous indumentum present between spines; ocrea very short, sometimes with a group of spines opposite the petiole; knee present; flagellum to c. 50 cm long; petiole absent in mature climbing stems, present in juveniles, up to 3 cm long; rachis 50–60 cm long, armed with scattered black tipped reflexed spines with swollen bases; leaflets narrow lanceolate, 15–17 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, the longest to 27 by 2 cm, the tips long acuminate, adaxially bright shiny green, abaxially paler with some very thin grey caducous indumentum, bristly along mid vein both adaxially and abaxially and along margins. Inflorescences to 1.3 m long, including a short terminal flagellum, the male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; partial inflorescences up to c. 11, c. 10–30 cm apart, up to 27 cm long; rachillae strongly curled, the male to 1.5 by 0.1 cm, mostly much shorter, the female 1–2.5 by 0.15 cm. Mature fruit rounded, c. 1.3 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.1 by 0.1 cm, and covered in 17 vertical rows of pale straw-coloured channelled scales with darker margins. Seed c. 1 by 1 by 0.7 cm, flattened laterally with a hollow at the chalaza, deeply grooved and almost brain-like; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf not recorded.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus godefroyi . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 360. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Slender clustering rattan. Stem without sheaths c. 0.5 cm diam., with sheaths 0.8 cm diam., internodes c. 15 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths bearing scattered solitary reflexed narrow triangular spines 0.2–0.6 by 0.1–0.15 cm with swollen bases, and thin caducous brown tomentum; knee well developed, unarmed; flagellum to 60 cm; petiole absent; rachis 20–30 cm long, bearing scattered, reflexed curved spines to 2 by 1.5 cm with black tips and swollen bases; leaflets broadly lanceolate, rather thin, 5–6 on each side of the rachis, the proximal 2–3 reflexed across the sheathed stem, the apical two joined for about one half their length, and forming a group of four with two more leaflets, the other leaflets very distant and somewhat irregularly arranged, basal leaflets 4–16 by 0.7–30 cm; middle leaflets 10.5–26 by 3–4.5 cm; apical leaflets 12–21 by 3–4.5 cm; upper surface of leaflets with conspicuous distant transverse veinlets, undersurface of leaflets covered in thin grey tomentum. Inflorescence flagelliform, only female known, to at least 112 cm long, with at least 2 partial inflorescences; bracts strictly tubular, tightly sheathing, with triangular tips and bearing scattered and rather sparse reflexed spines to 0.2 by 0.1 cm, with scattered brown indumentum between; partial inflorescences to at least 45 cm long, and 2–3 distant rachillae on each side; rachillae held ± at right angles, to 0.45 by 0.2 cm. Immature fruit ovoid to broadly ellipsoid, 0.7 by 0.4 cm with a beak 0.2 by 0.1 cm and covered in 20 vertical rows of pale brown scales with mid-brown margins and central marking and pale tips.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus griseus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 360. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Clustering moderate-sized rattan. Stems climbing to 20 m long, without sheaths 0.5–2 cm diam., with sheaths 13–30 cm diam., internodes up to 13–30 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; leaf sheaths dull green, very densely armed with upward pointing triangular, flattened dark brown to black spines of various lengths, 0.1–2.5 cm long, the largest with decurrent bases, bases in general rather swollen and pale, the margins often irregular and with abundant caducous pale brown indumentum on and between the spines, spines around the leaf sheath mouth much larger and longer than the rest, to 15 cm long, dark brown; knee present, armed as the rest of the sheath; ocrea 10–15 cm long or more, papery, mid-brown, soon disintegrating; flagellum to 0.75–3 m long; petiole 10–25 cm long, sparsely armed with dark brown reflexed spines to 0.5 cm; rachis 0.65–1.39 m, arcuate, armed with scattered and grouped refl exed hook-like spines; leaflets 35-50 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, rather widely spaced, the largest 25–45 by 1.7–2.2 cm, apical pair to 5 by 0.5 cm, very shortly joined near the base, adaxially with 3 veins bristly, abaxially the main vein bristly., Inflorescences 0.3–2.5 m long, the male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, with a terminal flagellum, and 2-8 partial inflorescences, each subtended by a conspicuous brown flattened papery open bract, tubular at its very base, sparsely to densely armed with short pale spines to 0.4 cm long; male rachillae crowded, to 1 by 0.2 cm, female rachillae to 10 by 0.3 cm. Fruit rounded, c. 0.7 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.15 by 0.1 cm and covered in 15–18 vertical rows of pale straw-coloured scales. Seed c. 0.5 cm diam., somewhat flattened on one side, the surface rugose; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf not recorded.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus guruba . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 361. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Slender clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 10 m long, without sheaths to 0.4–1 cm diam., with sheaths to 2 cm diam., internodes 5–18 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths green with reddish-brown indumentum, and bearing abundant scattered or partially grouped narrow triangular spines with swollen bases, the longest to 2 cm, the spine margins hairy, smaller spines often interspersed with larger ones, occasionally a few spines around the leaf sheath mouth larger than the rest, to 5 cm long and erect; ocrea inconspicuous, unarmed; knee conspicuous, generally unarmed; flagellum to 1 m; leaf rachis to 75 cm long, bearing up to 35 leaflets on each side, regularly arranged but usually with a few gaps; the longest 15–40 by 1.3–2 cm, covered with small bristles along the 3–5 prominent ribs adaxially and abaxially, margins bristly. Inflorescences with a terminal flagellum, and with up to 5 rather distant partial inflorescences; male and female inflorescences superficially similar, to 1.5 m long, the male branched to 2-3 orders, the female to 1-2 orders, each partial inflorescence to 12 cm long, composed of strongly adpressed rachillae 0.5-2.5 cm long, giving the whole partial inflorescence a spike-like appearance. Mature fruit broad ellipsoid, c. 1 by 0.7 cm, with a short beak, and covered with c. 17 vertical rows of straw-coloured scales with dark red margins. Seed rounded, c. 0.7 cm diam.; endosperm homogeneous.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus henryanus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 362. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Almost always solitary high-climbing slender to moderate-sized rattan, all parts drying pale straw-coloured. Stems to 20 m long, without sheaths to 1 cm diam., with sheaths to 2 cm diam., internodes to 18 cm or more long. Leaves ecirrate; sheath dull to bright green, densely armed with patent-orientated to slightly reflexed green spines to 2.5 cm long, with black tips and slightly swollen bases, scattered brown scales present between the spines; knee prominent; ocrea inconspicuous; flagellum to 2 m long; petiole absent or to 15 cm long; rachis to 80 cm long, it and the petiole armed with short triangular spines; leaflets c. 9 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged but generally very distant, very broad lanceolate, cucullate, of a very thick leathery texture, transverse veinlets very conspicuous, sinuous and close, apical leaflet pair usually joined along half their length, leaflet margins thickened. Inflorescences male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, flagellate to 2 m long, with up to 8 partial inflorescences; rachillae reflexed, the male to 2 by 0.3 cm, the female to 10 by 0.4 cm. Mature fruit ovoid or oblong in outline, to 1.2 by 0.7 cm, with a very conspicuous beak to 0.3 by 0.2 cm and covered in 22 vertical rows of pale yellowish-straw coloured scales. Seed c. 0.9 by 0.5 cm, slightly pitted; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf bifid, with broad shiny green leaflets with very conspicuous cross veins.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus insignis longispinosus. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 363. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Extremely variable slender to very slender clustering rattan forming low thickets or climbing. Stem to 10 m or more long, without sheaths 0.2–0.6 cm diam., with sheaths to 1 cm diam., internodes to 30 cm long, usually less. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths bright green when fresh, frequently reddish tinged, somewhat striate, unarmed or sparsely to densely armed with patent spines to 0.5 cm; knee present; ocrea moderately conspicuous, to 1 cm, deep crimson when young, tattering with age; flagellum to 1 m; petiole usually absent, rarely to 5 cm in some montane forms; leaflets 4–10 on each side of the rachis, grouped or more rarely subregular, lanceolate to spathulate, the lowermost 1–2 pairs often swept back across the stem, longest leaflets to 20 by 5 cm but usually much less, transverse veinlets conspicuous; young leaves tinged pink. Male and female inflorescences superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, with 2–5 partial inflorescences bearing crimson rachillae ± at right angles; male rachillae 3–5 by 0.2 cm, female rachillae 2–5 by 0.2 cm. Ripe fruit ovoid, c. 1.2 by 0.8 cm, with a short beak and covered in 15–21 vertical rows of pale greenish-white scales. Seed somewhat angular; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf with 4 broad shiny leaflets.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus javensis . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 364. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary (very rarely clustered) moderate rattan. Stems climbing to 30 m or more long, without sheaths 0.8–1 cm diam., with sheaths to 2 cm diam., internodes to 25 cm long. Leaves cirrate; sheaths dull to pale green, drying very pale brownish-green, armed with sparse patent ± triangular spines borne on swollen bases, sometimes also with very faint horizontal ridges, sometimes unarmed, and with brown scales abundant on young leaf surfaces; knee conspicuous; ocrea scarcely developed; flagellum absent; petiole absent; rachis to 35 cm long; cirrus to 65 cm long; leaflets c. 20 on each side of the rachis, concolorous, arranged irregularly, the basal up to 8 pairs on each side very close and strongly reflexed across the leaf sheaths forming a chamber in which ants frequently nest, upper leaflets in groups of 2–4 and fanned within the groups, the largest leaflets to c. 20 by 0.5–2 cm, somewhat plicate, drying very pale green. Inflorescences usually about the same length as the leaves, without a terminal flagellum, and with up to 10 partial inflorescences, the male branching to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; main bracts rather densely armed with black-tipped, pale, bulbous-based spines and brown indumentum, ultimate bracts and bracteoles with abundant minute spines producing a rough feel; male rachillae very short, to 0.5 by 0.1 cm, female rachillae to 7 by 0.2 cm. Mature fruit rounded, c. 1.2 cm diam., with a short beak and covered with 15–19 vertical rows of pale straw- to whitish-coloured scales, sometimes flecked with red. Seed rounded, c. 1 cm diam., deeply pitted; endosperm slightly ruminate. Seedling leaf bifid.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus laevigatus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 365. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Very robust clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 30 m long, usually less, without sheaths 3.5–5 cm diam., with sheaths 7–10 cm diam., internodes 10–45 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; leaf sheath dull green, densely armed with erect, spreading and reflexed flattened yellow-based spines of varying length, solitary or grouped in partial whorls, the longest to 6 cm long and 0.5 cm wide at base, interspersed with groups of much smaller needle-like spines, grey indumentum abundant between and on the spines; knee present but largely obscured by spines; ocrea inconspicuous; flagellum very robust, often to 10 m long; petiole 0.6–1.5 m long, densely armed with solitary and grouped blackish spines with yellow bases, of size similar to those on the sheath; rachis to 3 m long, yellowish-green, armed as the petiole; leaflets to c. 50 on each side of the rachis, irregularly arranged in groups of 2–7 and fanned within the groups, giving the whole leaf a plumose appearance, the longest to 75 by 4 cm, sharply spinulose along margins and upper-surface of mid vein and armed with black bristles to 2 cm long along mid vein on undersurface. Inflorescences flagellate, often to 10 m long, the male and female superficially similar, the male branching to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, with up to 12 rather distant partial infl orescences, the longest to over 1.5 m long; male rachillae to 10 by 0.4 cm long, female rachillae to 45 by 0.5 cm. Fruit turbinate, to 3.5 by 2 cm, with a triangular beak 0.4 cm long, and covered in c. 12 vertical rows of dull mid-brown, horizontally banded with darker brown unchannelled scales with laciniate margins. Seed c. 2.7 by 1.7 cm, endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf not recorded.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Solitary, massive high-climbing rattan. Stems ultimately reaching over 100 m long, but rarely attaining this due to overharvesting, without sheaths to 8 cm diam., sometimes very much more slender near the stem base (c. 2.5 cm diam.), with sheaths to 11 cm diam., internodes to 40 cm long, less in exposed stems from above the forest canopy. Leaf cirrate; sheaths dull grey green, densely armed with black, flattened, hairy-margined, patent or slightly reflexed, triangular spines, the largest to 3 by 1 cm, scattered or arranged in lateral groups, much smaller spines to 0.5 cm long abundant between the larger spines, thin white wax abundant between spines, particularly on newly emerged sheaths; knee conspicuous, armed as the rest of the sheath; ocrea ill-defined; flagellum absent; petiole to 12 by 5 cm, much longer in juveniles, armed as the rachis with short triangular grapnel spines and with scattered indumentum; rachis to 5 m long; cirrus to 3 m long; leaflets pale greyish-green, 45–60 on each side of the rachis, ± regularly arranged, limply pendulous and versatile in adult leaves, somewhat irregular and grouped, not obviously pendulous in juvenile leaves, margins with conspicuous black bristles. Inflorescences very robust, to c. 2.5 m long with numerous (up to 18) rather close partial inflorescences to 70 cm long, subtending bracts densely armed with spines to 0.3 cm long, the male inflorescence branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; male rachillae to 3 by 0.3 cm, the female to 15 by 0.5 cm. Mature fruit ovoid, to 2.8 by 2 cm, with a wide short beak to 0.3 by 0.3 cm, and covered with 15 vertical rows of yellowish scales with blackish-brown margins. Seed ovoid, to 1.8 by 1.2 cm, with finely pitted surface; endosperm densely and deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with 2 divergent cucullate leaflets with a grey-blue bloom on a dull green surface.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Robust clustering rattan. Stem climbing to great heights, to 50 m or more long, without sheaths to 4 cm diam., with rather prominent nodes and frequently slightly angular in cross section, with sheaths to 7 cm diam., internodes to 30 cm long. Leaves subcirrate; sheaths dark green, armed with large triangular, flattened, yellowish-based black spines to 4 by 1 cm, and scattered dull brown scales; knee conspicuous; ocrea short, quickly tattering; flagellum massive, to 10 m or more long, dark green, armed with short black, yellowish-based spines; petiole to 1 m (usually less); rachis to 3 m long; leaflets 20–30 on each side of the rachis, usually pale green, regularly arranged, the proximal to 50 by 5 cm increasing to 80 by 8 cm in the middle, decreasing to minute at the tip, c. 4 by 0.5 cm, the rachis tip forming a subcirrus, the leaflets drying pale green, not blackish, prickly on the upper surface of the veins near the tip and along the margins. Inflorescences to 8 m long including the long terminal flagellum, male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, bearing 4–6 partial inflorescences to 80 cm long; male rachillae slender 5–8 by 3 cm, female rachillae robust, reflexed, 10–18 by 0.4 cm. Male flower with 12 stamens. Ripe fruit ellipsoid, to 3 by 2 cm, tipped with a short beak and covered in 15 vertical rows of matt brown to black scales with paler bases. Seed to 2 by 0.8 cm, rather angular and grooved with one flattened lateral face; sarcotesta sour; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf bifid, shiny green.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus ornatus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 370. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary (very rarely clustering) rattan. Stem climbing to 10 m, without sheaths to 1.5 cm diam., with sheaths to 3 cm diam., internodes to 15 cm long. Leaf cirrate; sheaths bright green, rather densely armed with black, yellow-based flattened spines to 5 by 0.7 cm, upward-pointing, patent or reflexed; knee poorly developed, usually obscured by spines; ocrea tattering, inconspicuous; petiole to 30 cm long, armed with long black, yellowish-based spines; rachis arching, to 1.1 m or more long; cirrus to 60 cm long; leaflets to c. 50 on each side of the rachis, arranged in groups of 2–5 (rarely more), arcuate, dark shiny green except at the base where pale yellowish, 20–30 by 2–3 cm, ± unarmed. Inflorescences strongly curved, male and female superfi cially similar, the male branching to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, to 1.2 m, with c. 7 partial inflorescences, the longest to 40 cm; male rachillae to 3 cm long; female rachillae to 4 cm bearing rather distant flowers. Ripe fruit rounded, c. 1.2 cm diam., with conspicuous beak to 0.15 cm long, and covered in 12–13 vertical rows of yellowish scales with brown margins. Seed hemispherical, c. 0.9 cm diam., with superficial pitting; endosperm very sparsely and shallowly ruminate. Seedling leaf not recorded.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Moderate to robust clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 30 m long, without sheaths 0.3–3 cm diam., with sheaths 0.7–5 cm diam., internodes 15–30 cm long. Leaf cirrate; sheaths bright green, variably armed sparsely to densely with scattered, patent or slightly reflexed red-brown, yellow-based spines to 3 cm long, sometimes interspersed with much smaller broad-triangular dark spines, pale to reddish-brown caducous indumentum usually abundant on newly emerged sheaths, sometimes distinctly striped; knee conspicuous, usually more sparsely armed than the rest of the sheath; ocrea very inconspicuous, unarmed, soon disintegrating; flagellum absent; petiole 5–30 cm long, semi-circular in cross section, the adaxial surface often armed with short erect spines; rachis to 2.5 m or more; cirrus 0.4–1 m; leaflets 10–25 on each side of the rachis arranged in evenly spaced divergent pairs, a few leaflets near the base and the cirrus borne singly, the largest leaflets to 35 by 5.5 cm, rarely larger, tips somewhat cucullate, margins bristly, veins both adaxially and abaxially unarmed. Inflorescences male to 1.4 m long, the female usually much shorter, to 50 cm long, lacking a terminal flagellum, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, partial inflorescences 8–12, close and not very well differentiated; male rachillae 2.5–5 by 0.3 cm long, female rachillae to 10 by 0.4 cm. Fruit rounded, the calyx explanate at fruit maturity so fruit appearing sessile, 0.7–1.2 by 0.7–1 cm, with a short rather triangular reddish beak to 0.15 by 0.15 cm, and covered in 17 vertical rows of white unchannelled scales. Seed c. 0.5–0.9 by 0.5–0.7 cm, ± rounded; endosperm homogeneous.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Clustering slender rattan. Stem climbing to 15 m, without sheaths c. 0.6 cm diam., with sheaths to c. 1 cm diam., internodes c. 12 cm long. All parts drying dark brown. Leaf ecirrate; sheath dark green, armed with bulbous swellings, some of which ending in minute spines, pale brown indumentum scattered on sheath surface; knee conspicuous, often with a ring-like swelling below it; ocrea inconspicuous; flagellum to 80 cm long; petiole absent; rachis together with apical leaflets to 45 cm long, with up to 8 leaflets on each side of the rachis, the terminal pair joined for at least a quarter of their length, other leaflets somewhat irregularly arranged, dark green, said to smell of pandan when fresh, the longest to 25 by 3 cm. Inflorescence to 1 m long, male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, with up to 8 partial inflorescences, each with curving rachillae; male rachillae to 3 cm long, the female to 6 cm long. Flowers rather large, to 0.4 cm long. Fruit ± oblate, to 1.7 by 1.9 cm, covered in 23 vertical rows of pale brown scales. Seed c. 1 cm diam., endosperm deeply ruminate.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Calamus pandanosmus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 373. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary moderate to robust rattan. Stem climbing to 20 m tall or more, without sheaths c. 2 cm diam., with sheaths 3.5–7 cm diam., internodes 6–20 cm long. Leaf ecirrate; sheaths mid green with broad yellow streaks when fresh, pale brown when dry, armed with scattered large pale yellow green black-tipped flattened spines with conspicuous swollen yellowish bases and black hairy margins, the largest spines to 4 by 0.8 cm, much smaller spines often present between the large ones, sparse caducous brown indumentum present between spines; knee well developed, armed as the sheath, or sometimes unarmed; ocrea poorly developed; flagellum to 3.5 m long; all cut surfaces oozing yellow creamy gum; petiole 0.6–1.75 m long, armed with pale yellowish-green spines with black tips similar to those on sheath; rachis conspicuously arcuate, to 3.5 m long, armed with reflexed grapnel spines to 0.5 cm long; leaflets 30–50 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, rather stiff, the longest to 50 by 2–4 cm, main veins bristly on both surfaces, margins bristly near the leaflet tip. Inflorescences 3–6 m long, male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders with 2–3 partial inflorescences only, to 25 cm long, borne near the inflorescence base, and a long terminal flagellum; primary bracts conspicuous, splitting along part of their length and becoming flattened, tattering near their tips, armed with short triangular spines; male rachillae c. 3 by 0.2 cm, the female to 5 by 0.2 cm, flowers relatively large (to 0.75 cm long). Mature fruit globose to very slightly obovoid, borne on a stalked disc, to 2 by 1.6 cm, with a short beak to 0.2 by 0.1 cm, and covered in 15–16 vertical rows of bright reddish-brown, unchannelled scales. Seed globose, c. 1.5 cm diam., pitted; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with 4–6 very slender leaflets.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
