description: Solitary palm 3–5 m tall. Stem c. 5.5–7 cm diam. Leaf sheath 1.2–1.3 m long, extended in a chartaceous, c. 70 cm long ocrea; petiole up to 2.3 m long, armed basally with flattened, up to 0.7–0.8 cm long spines; blade divided into 33–35 segments; middle segment with 3 adaxial ribs, sometimes petiolulate, c. 75 cm long, the remaining segments with 2 adaxial ribs, the basal ones 48–52 cm long; indentations leading to the adaxial ribs 11–12 cm long, those leading to the abaxial ribs 4–6.5 cm long. Inflorescence up to 2.5 m long, with about six branched partial inflorescences; peduncle to 50 cm long; prophyll 25–30 cm long, to 3.5 cm wide; peduncular bract one, 25–30 cm long, splitting irregularly at the apex only; partial inflorescence with 3–5, up to 40 cm long rachillae. Flowers borne on c. 0.25 cm long pedicels, solitary, buds spindle-shaped, 1–1.1 by 0.35–0.4 cm; calyx 0.4–0.5 cm long; corolla 0.7–0.8 cm long, glabrous, cream white, reflexed at anthesis; filaments free distally, not forming a staminal ring. Fruit 1.5–1.7 by 1–1.2 cm, ovoid.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala distans . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 431. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary palm, usually less than 2 m tall. Stem 2–3 cm diam. Leaf sheath 12–15 cm long with ligule up to 15 cm long in young leaves; petiole up to 2.2 m long, basally with 0.2–0.3 cm long spines; blade divided into 19–21 segments; middle segment with 2–4 adaxial ribs, 30–55 cm long, sometimes with short petiolule, the remaining segments with one adaxial rib, the basal ones 35–40 cm long; indentations leading to the adaxial ribs 1–1.5 cm long, those leading to the abaxial ribs c. 0.5 cm long. Inflorescence 0.8–1.8 m long, with 6–11 branched partial inflorescences; peduncle 12–30 cm long; prophyll 15–25 cm long; peduncular bract lacking or one (rarely two), 15–25 cm long, with a 1–2 cm long split along one side; partial inflorescences with 3–7, 8–10 cm long rachillae. Flowers sessile on widened tubercles, solitary or in 2–3 flowered cincinni; buds 0.2–0.3 cm long, rounded to club–shaped; calyx 0.25–0.3 cm long; corolla 0.4–0.5 cm long, erect at anthesis, greenish to yellow; filaments fused to staminal ring, filament teeth longitudinally extending to c. 0.1 cm long at anthesis. Fruit 1.2–1.5 by 0.7–1 cm, ellipsoid.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala glabra . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 432. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary palm, acaulescent or with short stem no more than 1 m tall. Stem 4–7 cm diam. Leaf sheath 20–35 cm long with ligule up to 20 cm long in young leaves; petiole up to 200 cm long, basally with unevenly sized, irregularly spaced and up to 0.3 cm long spines; lamina divided into 11–19 unequally wide segments; middle segment with 14–16 adaxial ribs, 30–65 cm long, the remaining segments with 1–2 adaxial ribs, the basal ones 24–30 cm long; indentations of middle segment shallow, those of the remaining segments leading to the adaxial folds deeper, up to 2.5 cm. Inflorescence 20–70 cm long, with 2–4 partial inflorescences; peduncle 10–20 cm; prophyll 12–26 cm long, splitting cleanly along one side or in many places for 1–2 cm; peduncular bract lacking; rachis bracts up to 12 cm long basally; partial inflorescence unbranched or rarely with up to three rachillae, basally contained in the tubular rachis bract; rachillae 4–12 cm long. Flowers up to 60 on one rachilla, solitary or in pairs, on prominent 0.1–0.2 cm long pedicels, floral subtending bract triangular, inconspicuous; bud c. 0.5 by 0.3 cm, turbinate; calyx 0.15–0.2 cm long, loosely enclosing corolla in dried specimens, sparsely covered with golden hairs, membranous and striate, apically truncate to irregularly split; corolla 0.3–0.4 cm long, densely covered with simple golden hairs, lobes up to 0.2 cm long, erect at anthesis, creamy white; androecium 0.2–0.25 cm long, staminal ring c. 0.2 mm high, filaments shortly subulate; anthers reniform, c. 0.5 mm long; ovary 0.15–0.2 cm long, cylindrical, glabrous, rounded apically, style 0.15 cm long, overtopping the anthers at anthesis. Fruit globose, c. 1 cm diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala kunstleri . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 433. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary or clustering palm with 1–2 dominant shoots, acaulescent or with stems 1.5–2(–3) m tall. Stem 2–4 cm diam. Leaf sheath 30–40 cm long, ligule fragile; petiole up to 2.2 m long, basally with 0.2–0.3(–0.6) cm long, evenly distributed spines; lamina divided into 13–19 segments; middle segment with 3–4 adaxial ribs, 30–50 cm long, sometimes with 5–7 cm long petiolule, the remaining segments with 1–2 adaxial ribs, the basal ones 25–35 cm long, indentations leading to the adaxial folds 0.4–0.6 cm long in apical segment to 2 cm in basal segments, those leading to the abaxial folds to 0.5 cm long. Inflorescences 20–50 cm long, with 4–5 partial inflorescences; peduncle 10–20 cm long; prophyll 5–15 cm long, covered by ferruginous ramenta; peduncular bract lacking; proximal rachis bract 5–9 cm long, rounded, dry and woody towards the apex, with 1 to several splits up to 2 cm long; partial inflorescence branched to second order, basally contained inside the tubular rachis bract, with 2–5 rachillae; rachillae 2–12 cm long, curved to sinuous. Flowers up to 70 on longest rachillae, more or less distichously arranged, strictly solitary, borne on short pedicels, subtended by minute floral subtending bracts; bud 0.35–0.5 by 0.2–0.25 cm, ellipsoid; calyx cylindrical, 0.2–0.3 cm long, covered by scattered, minute translucent simple hairs, apically truncate with shallow, irregular splits or with bifi d lobes; corolla c. 0.35–0.4 cm long, densely covered by minute, more or less adpressed golden brown hairs, lobes c. 0.15 cm long; androecium fused to corolla for 0.2–0.25 cm, staminal ring c. 0.5 mm high, filaments subulate; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm long; ovary 0.18–0.2 cm long, fusiform, glabrous, often constricted at the middle, locules in lower half, apex tapered, style slender 0.1–0.12 cm long, not overtopping the anthers at anthesis. Fruit globose, c. 1 cm diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala malajana . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 434. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary palm tree. Stem usually less than 1 m tall, 5–8 cm diam., often covered by persistent leaf bases to the base. Leaf sheath 40–50 cm long, ligule up to 15 cm long in young leaves; petiole up to 2.2 m long, basally with 0.2–0.5 cm long, slender, often unevenly sized and irregularly set spines; lamina divided into 9–17 segments; middle segment entire with 7–17 adaxial ribs, or breaking up irregularly into up to three additional segments, petiolulate or rarely sessile, 35–65 cm long; the remaining segments with 2–4 adaxial ribs, the basal ones 30–50 cm long; indentations leading to adaxial and abaxial folds almost even, 0.2–0.5 cm. Inflorescence rarely more than 50 cm long, sinuous and messy looking, often partly covered by litter trapped at the leaf bases, with 4–6(–7) partial infl orescences; peduncle 10–15 cm long; prophyll 9–12 cm long; peduncular bracts lacking; basal rachis bract 8–15(–20) cm long, inflated distally, disintegrating irregularly at the apex; partial inflorescences with 3–6 rachillae, curved in various directions, with light brown to ferruginous woolly hair covering, proximal rachillae (5–)10–15 cm long. Flowers up to c. 150 on longest rachillae, grouped in 2–3 fl owered cincinni basally to solitary distally, sessile; bract subtending cincinni or individual flowers up to 0.5 cm; calyx 0.25–0.4 cm long, urn-shaped, glabrous basally, covered by light brown woolly hair above the middle, with three rounded c. 0.5 mm long lobes; corolla 0.3–0.4 cm long, covered by seriate hairs arranged in transversal stripes, erect at anthesis, greenish-brown on the outside, bright yellow on the inside; androecium c. 0.15 cm long, fused to corolla for 0.5 mm; anthers 0.6–0.8 mm long: ovary 0.15 cm long, obovoid, locules in lower half, style c. 0.5 mm, stigma overtopping anthers. Fruit rounded, 0.8–1 cm diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala merguensis . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 434. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Medium-sized palm, solitary to caespitose with 1–3 dominant stems up to 3 m tall. Stem 2–3 cm diam., with numerous suckers at base. Leaf sheath 10–20 cm long; petiole up to 1.2 m long, armed basally with narrowly triangular spines, spreading to reflexed, up to 0.5 cm long; lamina divided into a variable number of segments, 7–22, these equal-sized with 3–5 adaxial ribs in many-segmented leaves to middle segment largest with 8–18 adaxial ribs in few-segmented leaves; middle segment 25–32 cm long; indentations leading to the adaxial folds c. 2 cm long on middle segment, to 3 cm long on remaining segments. Inflorescence 22–57 cm long, with 1–5 partial inflorescences; peduncle 21–41 cm long; prophyll to c. 25 cm long; peduncular bracts lacking; rachis bracts chartaceous, basal ones splitting deeply, to 17 cm, mouth loosely sheathing; partial inflorescences often branching near the mouth of the rachis bract, with 1–4 rachillae; rachillae 7–14 cm long. Flowers solitary or gathered in cincinni of 2–3, on up to 0.5 mm, hairy stalks; calyx cylindrical with a slight constriction just above base, 0.25–0.3 cm long, wide and flattened basally, apex truncate to irregularly lobed, covered with scattered to dense coarse tawny golden brown hairs; corolla 0.45–0.5 cm long, densely covered with fine adpressed golden brown simple hairs, lobes 0.25–0.35 cm long; androecium with c. 0.5 mm high staminal ring; filaments filiform with triangular base, 0.05–0.1 cm long, anthers reniform, c. 0.8 mm long; ovary glabrous, cylindrical with rounded apex, c. 0.2 cm long; style filiform, 0.12 cm long. Fruit globose, c. 0.9 cm diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala modesta . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 435. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Caespitose palm, with up to 7 m tall stems. Stem 5–7 cm diam. Leaf sheath to 40 cm long, with ligule up to 10 cm long in young leaves; petiole up to 2.5 m long, ranging in colour from greenish-brown to orange brown, basally armed with 0.2–0.3(–0.5) cm long rounded spines, straight or curved, evenly sized, inserted more or less regularly; lamina divided into 8–12 more or less equal, 47–88 cm long segments, the middle one with 6–8 adaxial ribs, split to 8–15 cm above the base in two truncate lobes, the remaining ones with 2–7 adaxial ribs, indentations leading to the adaxial folds 2–3 cm long, those leading to the abaxial folds c. 0.5 cm long. Inflorescence 1.5–2 m long, with 6–7 partial inflorescences; peduncle 25–50 cm long, prophyll 25–30 cm long covered with a mixture of ferruginous ramenta and stellate hairs; peduncular bracts 1–2; rachis bracts splitting cleanly at the apex in a few irregular sized teeth 0.5–1 cm long; partial inflorescences with 4–8 rachillae; longest rachillae 12–20 cm long. Flowers up to 150 on one rachilla, mostly solitary but also in cincinni of 2–3, sessile; floral subtending bract to 0.5 mm long, deltoid; buds 0.25–0.3 cm long; calyx c. 0.2 cm long, glabrous, almost truncate apically, with three short, pointed teeth; corolla 0.25–0.3 cm long, drying striate, glabrous, erect, greenish; androecium 0.15–0.18 cm long, staminal ring 0.3–0.5 mm high, filaments filiform 0.1–0.2 mm long; anthers 0.4–0.5 mm long; ovary c. 0.1 cm long, glabrous, turbinate, truncate apically, filling about half the lumen inside flower, locules three times longer than wide, central in each carpel, style slender, filiform, c. 0.1 cm long, not overtopping the anthers. Fruit globose, 0.6–0.8 cm diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala paludosa . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 436. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary palm. Stem usually less than 2 m tall, c. 10 cm diam., often covered by old, black spine-like leaf bases. Leaf sheath 50–60 cm long; petiole up to 2.7 m long, armed in entire length with up to 1.5 cm long, flattened, recurved spines; lamina divided into a varying number of up to 21 segments, this number being relatively constant throughout a population, with translucent specks visible with backlighting at 10x; segments in divided leaves 50–90 cm long; indentations leading to the adaxial ribs 0.3–1.5 cm long, those leading to the abaxial ribs 2–6 cm long in basal segments to less than 2 cm in apical segment. Inflorescences up to 3.5 m long, with about seven, spicate, pendent, partial inflorescences; peduncle to 1.2 m long; prophyll 35–40 cm long; peduncular bract one, 33–36 cm long, covered with scattered minute ramenta, green to dry and woody distally, splitting irregularly, often with narrow rim of fibrous mesh; basal 2nd order rachis on up to 15 cm long bare basal portion and a 35–55 cm long flower-bearing portion. Flowers up to 200 on longest rachilla, solitary; floral subtending bract c. 0.25 cm long; pedicel c. 0.2 cm long, hairy; buds ventricose to obclavate in outline, 1.3–1.4 by 0.5–0.6 cm; calyx 0.6–0.7 cm long, campanulate, truncate with irregular indentations, not fused with receptacle; corolla 1–1.2 cm long, sericeous, reflexed at anthesis, on the inside white to green apically; androecium 0.8–0.9 cm long, fused basally with corolla in basal c. 0.5 cm, the remaining part of the filament free, anthers elongate, 0.3–0.35 cm long; ovary 0.2–0.3 cm long at anthesis, barrel-shaped, truncate, glabrous, style slender 0.7–0.8 cm long. Fruit ellipsoid, 1.2–1.9 by 0.9–1 cm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala peltata peltata. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 437. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Differing from the typical variety only in its unsegmented leaf.

description: Caespitose palm, 4–8 stemmed, individual stems up to 2.5 m tall, 2.8–3 cm diam. below the crown and with 0.5–1 cm long internodes. Leaves 10–12 in crown, sheath margins disintegrating into fibrous mesh; petiole 1.2–1.5 m long, armed on lower 30–50 cm, with more or less evenly distributed, irregularly sized, up to 0.3 cm long, straight spines; leaf blade divided into 11–15 segments, with slightly curved to straight lateral margins, converging basally in funnellike manner, middle segment sessile, undivided, 35–45 cm long, with 9–11 adaxial ribs, lateral segments of more or less equal length, with 3 or 4 adaxial ribs, basal segments 30–35 cm long, obliquely truncate; indentations leading to adaxial ribs 0.5–1 cm long, those leading to abaxial splits 0.2–0.5 cm long. Inflorescences 80–90 cm long, carrying 4 or 5 partial inflorescences; peduncle 60 cm long; prophyll 30 cm long; basal rachis bract up to 27 cm long, covered with patches of ferruginous ramenta loosely fitting, irregularly splitting; basal partial inflorescence with 1–3, up to 12 cm long rachillae. Flowers shortly pedicellate, somewhat triquetrous, 0.7–0.75 cm long, borne in pairs almost throughout the rachilla, each pair subtended by an inconspicuous up to 0.5 mm long bract; calyx 0.48–0.5 cm long, unevenly tomentose, with rounded to truncate lobes; corolla 0.5–0.55 cm long; androecium fused to corolla for 0.22–0.23 cm, staminal ring c. 0.1 cm high. Fruits unknown.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala pitta . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 439. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary or caespitose palm, usually with one, up to 5 m tall stem, suckering at the base, 3–5 cm diam., covered by leaf sheath remnants distally. Leaf sheath 30–40 cm long, with ligule up to 15 cm long in young leaves; petiole 80–150 cm long, basal ¼ with up to 0.4 cm long spines; lamina divided into 9–11 segments; middle segment with 9–11 adaxial ribs, 40–55 cm long, the remaining segments decreasing gradually in width towards the base, here with 3–4 adaxial ribs, 30–45 cm long; indentations of middle and lateral segments leading to the adaxial ribs c. 1 cm long, those leading to the abaxial ribs c. 0.5 cm long, indentations of basal segments more irregular. Inflorescence 1–1.5 m long, with 5–7 unbranched partial inflorescences; peduncle 20–30 cm long; prophyll 20–30 cm long, loosely fitting, splitting irregularly to tattering apically; peduncular bract lacking; rachis 80–120 cm long; proximal rachis bracts 25–29 cm long, tubular, loosely fitting, inserted up to 40 cm below the divergence point of the partial inflorescences subtended; basal partial inflorescence 8–15 cm long, displaced above or hidden inside subtending bract, strongly zig-zagged to straight, narrowly diverging from rachis, densely covered with felt-like indumentum of stellate hairs. Flowers up to 40–60 on longest rachillae, solitary, rarely in pairs, sessile, subtended by c. 0.6 mm long, sparsely hairy, deltoid bracts; buds 0.7–0.9 cm long, bullet-shaped, often with a more or less oblique base; calyx to 0.7 cm long on longest(abaxial) side, basally covered with patches of ferruginous ramenta, to striate distally when dried, with 3 obtuse to rounded lobes up to 0.5 mm long; corolla c. 0.6 cm long, with minute ferruginous ramenta on exposed parts, erect at anthesis, yellow-greenish on lower ¾ and brown distally; androecium 0.25–0.3 cm long, fused to corolla for 0.1–0.15 cm, filaments to 0.1 cm long, narrowly deltoid; anthers elongate, 0.22–0.24 cm long, pointed apically; ovary c. 0.15 cm long, obovoid, tapering distally, locules in lower ½ to ¾; style slender, c. 0.15 cm long, stigma amidst the anthers. Fruit 0.9–1.2 cm diam., globose.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Licuala poonsakii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 441. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary, acaulescent palm. Stem short subterranean. Leaf: petioleto 90 cm long, scarcely armed in basal 10 cm, spines c. 0.2 cm long, recurved and set more or less regularly 1 cm apart; lamina divided into 3–4 gently curved segments, converging basally in a funnel-like fashion, middle segment c. 32 cm long, with 19 adaxial ribs, slightly curved lateral margins, rounded apically and c. 12 cm wide, the remaining segments 15–20 cm long, with 2–5 adaxial ribs, narrowly wedge-shaped to linear, obliquely truncate apically; indentations leading to the adaxial folds c. 0.5 cm long in middle segment, to 2 cm long in remaining segments, those leading to the abaxial folds less than 0.5 cm long. Infl orescence patent, shorter than leaves, c. 30 cm long, with 2–3 partial inflorescences; peduncle c. 18 cm long; prophyll loosely sheathing; peduncular bracts absent; rachis c. 12 cm long; basal rachis bract c. 8 cm long, inflated in distal half; partial inflorescences spicate, inserted up to 8 cm above the mouth of their subtending bracts; rachillae up to 8 cm long, 0.1–0.2 cm diam., rigid, straight to slightly zig-zagged, narrowly diverging from rachis, densely covered with deciduous ferruginous felt-like hairs. Flowers in groups of up to 5(–7) on slightly swollen tubercles (prominent in fruiting specimens), solitary towards the apex; calyx cylindrical, 0.26–0.32 cm long, chartaceous, covered with scattered 0.4–0.7 mm long simple hairs, splitting neatly into three pointed lobes; corolla c. 0.25–0.32 cm long, rather thick, covered with patent white hairs in upper two thirds, glabrescent towards the base, lobes c. 0.2 cm long with acuminate apex; androecium with c. 0.5–0.7 mm long, truncate staminal ring; filaments filiform, c. 0.3 mm long; anthers reniform, c. 0.5 mm long; ovary 1–1.5 mm long turbinate to club-shaped, densely covered with coarse silky white hairs mostly on upper parts, style filiform, 0.1 cm long. Fruit globose, c. 0.8–1 cm diam.

description: Solitary palm, rarely suckering. Stem to 1 m tall, 1.7–2 cm diam., smooth, inconspicuously ringed. Leaf sheath 5–8 cm long on older leaves, with ligule up to 10 cm long; petiole 15–30 cm long, basally with few, scattered spines to 0.1–0.2 cm long; lamina thin chartaceous, often with a crumpled appearance, unevenly divided into 4–5 segments, with convexly curved lateral margins and converging basally in a funnel-like fashion; middle segment entire, with 13–14 adaxial ribs, 15–20 cm long, the remaining segments with 3–5 adaxial ribs, 15–77 cm long; indentations leading to the adaxial folds to c. 1.2 cm long, those leading to the abaxial folds c. 0.4 cm long. Inflorescences 15–34 cm long, patent to pendulous, spicate to furcate; peduncle c. 25–30 cm long; prophyll 17–22 cm long, inflated, with 6 cm long split along one side; peduncular bract lacking; rachis sinuous, almost glabrous; single rachis bract 2–5 cm long, loosely sheathing at the apex, inserted c. 3 cm above prophyll, sparsely covered with stellate hairs, splitting cleanly along one side; partial inflorescence spicate or branching near the apex of the subtending bract into two, 3–5 cm long rachillae, covered with simple, whitish to golden hairs. Flowers light green, solitary or in cincinni of 2(–3), on hairy floral stalks up to 0.1 cm long; floral subtending bracts c. 0.5 mm long; buds c. 0.35 cm long, turbinate; calyx c. 0.15 cm long, membranous, loosely enclosing corolla in dried specimens, striate, truncate apically, covered with dense to scattered fine golden hairs; corolla to 0.3–0.4 cm long, thick, striate when dried, covered with scattered fine brown simple hairs, lobes c. 0.2 cm long, apex acute; androecium c. 0.5 mm long; filaments filiform, c. 0.5 mm long, with triangular base; anthers reniform, c. 0.8 mm long; ovary glabrous, cylindrical, apex rounded, c. 0.1 cm long; style filiform, c. 0.15 cm long; stigma overtopping the anthers. Fruit c. 0.5 cm diam., globose.

description: Caespitose palm, with up to 4 m tall stems forming large clumps. Individual stems 4–5 cm diam., ringed by leaf scars. Leaf sheath to 40 cm long, with ligule up to 10 cm long, in younger leaves with dense cover of ferruginous to hyaline ramenta; petiole variable in length up to 2.5 m in fully developed leaves, armed almost to the distal end, armature variable but usually quite noticeable; lamina divided into 15–19 segments, 44–72 cm long; the middle segment sessile or with a petiolule to 6 cm long, with 5–9 adaxial ribs, the remaining ones with 1–3 adaxial ribs, indentations leading to the adaxial folds 1–4 cm long, those leading to the abaxial folds 0.5–1 cm long. Inflorescence 0.9–2.5 m long, extended above the crown, with 5–9 partial inflorescences; peduncle 20–50 cm long, for a large part hidden in prophyll; prophyll 20–30 cm long, covered with patches of ferruginous ramenta; peduncular bracts absent or present; rachis bracts dark green to brown distally, tubular, similar to the prophyll in texture and hair-covering, splitting irregularly into up to 2.5 cm long teeth or disintegrated apically; partial inflorescence inserted 2–6 cm above mouth of subtending bract, covered with dense, puberulent tomentum of simple, ferruginous to hyaline hairs; rachillae 2–7; longest rachilla 20–40 cm long. Flowers up to 200 on one rachilla, solitary or in 2(–3)-flowered cincinni; floral subtending bract to 0.5 mm long, deltoid; buds c. 0.3 cm long; calyx cylindrical to cyathiform, c. 0.3 cm long, covered with adpressed to patent hairs, apex with 0.1–0.13 cm long, obtuse to acuminate lobes; corolla 0.35–0.4 cm long, exposed parts densely covered by seriate hairs arranged in stripes towards the apex, light beige to white on the inside; androecium 0.25–0.3 cm long, staminal ring white 0.1–0.13 cm high, truncate, filaments subulate 0.3–0.4 mm long; anthers c. 0.5 mm long, elliptic; ovary c. 0.1 cm long, glabrous, turbinate, truncate apically, filling little less than half the lumen of the inside flower, locules 0.5–0.6 mm long, basally in each carpel, style slender, filiform, 0.12–0.13 cm long. Fruit globose, c. 0.8 cm diam.

description: Solitary, acaulescent palm. Stem subterranean, with very short internodes, J-shaped in older individuals, c. 2 cm diam. Leaf sheath 3–7 cm long in older leaves, sometimes with 1–2 cm long, caducous ligule; petiole 15–70(–90) cm long, lower ½ to ⅔ armed with 0.2–0.3(–0.5)cm long, spines; lamina divided into 3–11 unequal segments, converging basally in a funnel-like fashion, with translucent rounded specks visible with backlighting at 10x, scattered to numerous and in characteristic groups; middle segment 15–21(–30) cm long, with (10–)12–17 adaxial ribs, apically curved to rounded, middle 1–3 segments sessile, often inserted on up to 5 cm long petiolule, lateral and basal segments (14–)17–30 cm long, with (1–)3–5 adaxial ribs; indentations leading to the adaxial folds 0.5–0.7(–1.5) cm long, those leading to the abaxial folds c. 0.2–0.5 cm long. Inflorescence 15–25(–40) cm long, with 2–4 partial inflorescences; peduncle 7–15(–20) cm long; prophyll 3–5 cm long, often hidden in axil of the subtending leaf, covered with minute ramentose to stellate hairs, splitting cleanly along keels; peduncular bract one, 4–7 cm long, splitting cleanly but in 3–4 irregular teeth; rachis 8–10(–20) cm long; rachis bracts similar to peduncular bracts; unbranched and branched portion of partial inflorescence short; rachillae to 2–3, longest one 3–8 cm long, more or less zig-zagged. Flowers up to 20 on one rachilla, sessile, solitary or in pairs; floral subtending bract minute to lacking; buds ellipsoid, 0.35–0.4 cm long; calyx 0.2–0.25 cm long, vase-shaped, thickened basally, membranous distally, covered with simple ferruginous hairs, neatly split in three rounded, c. 0.1 cm long apically pointed lobes; corolla 0.3–0.35 cm long, covered by minute hairs on upper ⅔, white, erect to slightly recurved at anthesis; androecium 0.22–0.25 cm long, fused to corolla for 0.18–0.2 cm, staminal ring 0.4–0.5 mm high, filaments subulate, 0.2–0.3 mm long; anthers 0.4–0.5 mm long; ovary 1–1.3 cm long, obovoid, densely covered on upper half with minute adpressed white hairs, locules three times longer than wide, central in each carpel, style slender, c. 0.08–0.1 cm long, slightly overtopping the anthers. Fruit globose, 0.8–1 cm diam.

description: Tall palm trees, solitary, hermaphrodite or occasionally functionally dioecious (Australian-New Guinean species). Stem erect, ringed, basally with persistent leaf bases. Crown more or less globose, with skirt of dead leaves. Leaf palmate to costapalmate, induplicate; petiole elongate, armed along margins, usually with robust spines; adaxial hastula conspicuous, abaxial hastula poorly developed to absent; blade splitting along adaxial ribs, usually into single-fold segments. Inflorescence interfoliar; branched to 4 orders; peduncle elongate, peduncular bracts lacking or one; rachis longer than peduncle; rachis bracts loosely tubular like the peduncular bract; partial inflorescences (first order branches) 3–9, decreasing in size towards the distal nodes. Flowers inserted in groups of 3–6; stamens 6, fused to the corolla basally forming a cuplike structure; gynoecium united apically in slender style. Fruit one-seeded, greenish-blue, leaden blue to purple at maturity, globose to elliptical, more than 1 cm long; epicarp smooth, mesocarp fleshy; endocarp bony. Seed with homogeneous endosperm penetrated by an intrusion of the seed coat. Germination remote-tubular.</br></br>Twenty five species in NE tropical Africa, S Yemen, Bangladesh to Japan and Australia. Three species in Thailand.

description: Palm tree up to 20 m tall. Stem 25–30 cm diam. Crown with 30–50 leaves. Leaf sheath 50–60 cm long, breaking up in fibrous mesh; petiole 200–260 cm long, armed with basally swollen, up to 2 cm long, recurved spines; blade almost circular, flattened at first, becoming wavy, 2.6–2.8 m long, divided into 90–100 single-fold segments, lustrous green above, glaucous green below. Inflorescence branched to 3 orders, peduncle 25–30 cm long, prophyll 30–45 cm long, peduncular bract partly contained within prophyll; rachis 120–130 cm long, first order branches 4–6, with numerous, 10–30 cm long, rigid rachillae. Flowers in clusters of 3–5, sepals 0.2–0.4 cm long, petals 0.3–0.4 cm long. Fruit 2.5–3 cm long, globose to reniform, leaden blue. Seed coat intrusion apical.

description: Palm up to 40 m tall. Stem 40–65 cm diam. Crown with 25–30 leaves. Leaf sheath 25–30 cm, breaking up in mesh of coarse fibres; petiole 150–200 cm long, armed with strongly recurved, brown spines, largest on proximal portion, up to 6 cm long; blade divided ¼ to ¾ of radius into 80–90 single-fold, further divided almost to the hastula into groups of 2–12 segments, segment tips pendulous, light green on both sides. Inflorescence branched to 4 orders, 1.5–2.5 m long; first order branches 6–9; rachillae numerous, 15–45 cm long, pendulous, yellow. Flowers in clusters of 3–5, 0.15–0.2 cm long. Fruit reniform, globose to slightly ellipsoid, 1.5–2.5 cm long, glossy blue to blackish. Seed coat intrusion lateral.

description: Palm tree up to 25 m tall. Stem 20–30 cm diam.; crown with 30–60 leaves. Leaf sheath 40–50 cm long, extending in up to 20 cm long ligules; petiole 1.4–1.9 m long, armed basally with proximally swollen, up to 2.5 cm long, recurved spines; blade almost circular, wavy, 2–2.1 m long, divided into 90–110 single-fold segments, lustrous green above, glaucous green below. Inflorescence branched to 4 orders; peduncle c. 50 cm long; prophyll c. 30 cm long; peduncular bracts partly contained within prophyll; rachis 1–1.2 m long, first order branches 5–8; second order branches up to 26 on one first order branch; rachillae numerous, up to 22 cm long. Flowers in clusters of 5–7, sessile on small tubercles, sepals 0.1–0.2 cm long, petals 0.25–0.4 cm long. Fruit elliptic to obovoid, 2.5–3.5 cm long, lustrous bluish-green. Seed coat intrusion lateral.

description: Shrubby, acaulescent to short-stemmed, clustering palms. Leaf palmate, induplicate; sheath disintegrating into long persistent, coarse fibres; petiole elongate, unarmed; adaxial hastula distinct, triangular, shallow, with erose margin, abaxial hastula obscure; blade splitting for half to two thirds their radius along the adaxial ribs into numerous, single-fold segments, these shallowly indented at the tip. Inflorescence interfoliar; branched to 1–3 orders; peduncular bracts 1–3; rachis bracts tubular with triangular limbs. Flowers small, hermaphrodite or unisexual, inserted in groups of 2–3 or solitary; stamens 6, fused to form a shortly epipetalous, staminal tube; gynoecium of three free carpels, shortly united basally, hairy distally, with triangular styles. Fruit one-seeded, globose to ellipsoid, less than 1 cm diam.; epicarp silky hairy in young stages; mesocarp thin, fleshy; endocarp poorly developed. Seed with homogeneous endosperm, intrusion of the seed coat lateral and shallow. Germination remote; eophyll very narrow, strap-shaped.</br></br>Three species in Peninsular Thailand to Peninsular Malaysia. Two species in Thailand.

description: Clustering dioecious palm, rarely with more than 10 stems. Stem up to 3(–5) m tall at maturity, c. 5 cm diam., naked proximally, with close leaf sheath scars and vertical cracking, covered distally for 1-2 m with persistent, spine-like leaf sheath fibres. Leaf: petiole up to (20–)30–50(–70) cm long, cross section subcircular basally to oval distally, 0.3–0.5 cm diam.; blade rounded in outline, flattened, up to 75 cm diam., spilt into 25-30 single-fold segments, splits longest about ½ radius in the distal part, individual segments with 1–5 cm long indentations, pale green above, covered with thin white wax below. Inflorescence 25–40 cm long, with 3–5 first order branches rachillae to 4 cm long; male inflorescence branched to three orders, male flowers solitary or in groups; female inflorescence branched to 2 orders, flowers solitary. Flower c. 0.25 cm long, male flower with 0.1 cm long staminal tube and 0.5 mm long pistillode; female flower with flattened, c. 0.3 mm long staminodes and c. 0.15 cm long gynoecium. Fruit narrowly ovoid, c. 0.8 by 0.4 cm, yellowish-brown at maturity.

description: Clustering hermaphrodite palm, with up to 4 stems. Stem up to 7 m tall at maturity, c. 8 cm diam., naked proximally, with close leaf sheath scars, covered distally for 1–2 m with persistent leaf sheath fibres, remaining connected in the ligule-shaped tips. Leaf: petiole up to 70 cm long, more or less terete throughout, c. 0.5 cm diam.; blade rounded in outline, flattened, up to 25–40 cm diam., deeply split into 25–30 single-fold segments, individual segments shortly indented, greyish-green above, somewhat paler below with scattered brown dots. Inflorescence 70-90 cm long, rachillae numerous 7–12 cm long, minutely puberulous when young. Flowers solitary or inserted in groups of 2–3, bisexual, c. 0.2 by 0.15 cm, stamen filaments fused into a conspicuous c. 0.25 cm long tube, shortly adnate to corolla basally, gynoecium c. 0.1 cm long, densely covered by silky hairs. Fruit globose to ovoid, up to 1 by 0.5 cm, brown at maturity.

description: Clustering high-climbing dioecious hapaxanthic rattan with moderate to robust stems. Sheaths without knees; ocrea absent; flagellum absent. Leaf cirrate, bearing entire ± regularly arranged concolorous leaflets. Inflorescences produced simultaneously in the axils of the uppermost leaves, male and female superficially similar; primary axis branching to 3 orders, the branches bearing tubular triangular-tipped bracts subtending clusters of 2–7 flowers. Flowers: male flower with tubular calyx with 3 triangular lobes and 3 petals joined at the base; stamens 6, borne on the petals; pistillode minute; female flower with tubular calyx with 3 very short obtuse lobes, and corolla with 3 lobes; staminodes 6 epipetalous; ovary tipped with 3 small divergent stigmas; calyx enlarging considerably and splitting irregularly, persisting to mature fruiting; corolla also persistent. Mature fruit tipped with minute stigmatic remains, covered in minute irregularly arranged scales giving the fruit surface the appearance of sharkskin. Seed with thin sarcotesta; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf bifid.</br></br>One species in Indo-China to Sumatra.

description: Robust clustering thicket-forming dioecious rattan. Stems to 40 m or more long, without sheaths to 4 cm diam., with sheaths to 7 cm diam., internodes to 40 cm long in juvenile stems, 15–20 cm in exposed adult stems. Leaves cirrate; sheaths sparsely to densely covered in red brown scales, juvenile stems with distant whorls or partial whorls of robust slightly reflexed pale spines to 4 cm long, the whorls 6–7 cm apart, mature sheaths with far fewer spines, usually in groups of 2–7 in distant horizontal rows; knee absent; ocrea absent; petiole 5–30 cm long, longest in juvenile stems; rachis to 3 m long, covered in abundant reddish-brown indumentum; cirrus 1.5–2 m long; leaflets up to 30 on each side of the rachis, ± regularly arranged or in groups of 2–3, the longest to 45 by 5 cm, not bristly, shiny green adaxially, bright green abaxially. Inflorescences produced simultaneously from the topmost reduced leaves, the stems dying after flowering and fruiting, branching to 3 orders, male and female superficially similar, to 75 cm long with up to 25 pendulous or twisted partial inflorescences to 30 cm long, all axes covered in closely sheathing brown bracts with triangular tips. Mature fruit rounded or slightly oblate, c. 3 cm diam., with small black stigmatic remains, and covered with minute greenish scales. Seed rounded, slightly flattened at the base, c. 2.2 by 1.8 cm, the surface smooth, sarcotesta very thin; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf bifid.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Small to moderate sized, solitary or clustering, monoecious palms. Stem slender with green internodes and distinct leaf scars at least distally, basally often with cone of adventitious roots. Leaf sheath tubular, forming a well-defined crownshaft; petiole well developed, unarmed; blade pinnately divided into several, single-folded leaflets, these reduplicate, evenly spaced, inserted in one plane, linear to sigmoid, acute or acuminate, sometimes and especially the apical ones joined with only a short indentation at the tip. Inflorescence protandrous, in Thai species infrafoliar, pendulous, branching to 1(–2) orders, sheathed in bud by thin, membranous prophyll; peduncular bracts incomplete; rachillae basally with protandrous triads of one central female flower and two lateral male flowers, distally with solitary or paired male flowers. Flowers sessile, cream white; male flower slightly longer than female flower, fleshy, with 6 free stamens, elongate anthers, and no pistillode; female flower with no or minute staminodes; gynoecium globose, uniloculate, stigmas three, sessile. Fruiting and flowering rachillae not distinctly different in colour; fruit ovoid, epicarp smooth; mesocarp thin, fleshy; endocarp composed of longitudinal fibres. Seed with deeply ruminate endosperm. Germination adjacent ligular.</br></br>Five species in S Indo-China to W Malesia. Two species and one variety in Thailand.

description: Solitary palm. Stem 2–6 m tall, 4–6 cm diam. Leaves up to 7 in crown; sheath 20–45 cm long, forming a green to yellowish, swollen, up to 60 cm long crownshaft; petiole 10–55 cm long, blade 1.5–2 m long with up to 30 pinnae per side, longest ones in the middle, 30–65 cm long. Inflorescence branched to first order; peduncle 2–4 cm long; rachillae 3–4(–5), 25–40 cm long. Male flowers 0.6–1.3 cm long, calyx of male flower shorter than or equal to the corolla; female flowers with sepals 0.4–0.6 cm long, equal to or shorter than the petals. Fruit ellipsoid, 3–4 by 1.3–1.7 cm, with up to 0.3 cm long stigmatic remains, purplish black at maturity.

description: Clustering palm. Individual stems 3–5 m tall, 3–6 cm diam. Leaves 5–7 in crown; leaf sheath 25–60 cm long, forming a green to yellowish, slightly swollen, up to 80 cm long crownshaft; petiole 4–50 cm long; blade 2–3 m long with up to 30 pinnae per side, longest ones in the middle, 35–70 cm long. Inflorescence branched to first order; peduncle 1.5–3 cm long; rachillae 2–4, 20–35 cm long. Male flowers 1.2–1.6(–2) cm long, calyx of male flower much longer than the corolla; female flower with sepals 0.3–0.4 cm long, equal to or slightly longer than the petals. Fruit ellipsoid, 2.5–3 by 1–1.5 cm, with up to 0.2 cm long stigmatic remains, with erect lobes, brick red at maturity.

description: Differs from the typical variety on West Java by having fruits that are 2.5–3 cm long (as opposed to 1.5–2 cm long), tipped by a trilobed stigma (as opposed to cushion-shaped stigma), ripening brick red (as opposed to orange brown) and drying with longitudinal ridges (as opposed to broad, shallow dimples).

description: Creeping, moderate sized palm, monoecious. Stem prostrate to subterranean, branching dichotomously, distinctively stepped by curved leaf scars; crown of few large, erect leaves. Leaf sheath splitting cleanly to the base, glabrous; petiole elongate, wide and channelled above proximally to rounded in cross section distally, unarmed; blade pinnately divided into numerous, regularly distributed, single-fold, reduplicate pinnae; individual pinnae coriaceous, apically acute, with prominent midrib bearing large, brown bifurcating ramenta, transverse veinlets inconspicuous. Inflorescence protogynous, interfoliar, erect, branching to 4-6 orders; peduncle elongate; prophyll, peduncular bract and rachis bracts tubular, splitting longitudinally, leathery brown; rachis shorter than peduncle; female flowers gathered in a single terminal head (rarely more), male rachillae borne on third to fifth order branches below, at male anthesis often overtopping the terminal head of female flowers; female flowers densely inserted on club-shaped apex on the inflorescence; perianthparts free; staminodes lacking; carpels three, free, much longer than perianth; asymmetrically urn-shaped with more or less lateral, funnel-shaped stigmatic opening; male flowers densely inserted on catkin-like rachillae, perianth similar to female flowers; stamens three, filaments and connective connate into a common stalk; pistillode lacking. Fruits aggregated in head-like structure, compressed and irregularly angled; epicarp smoooth; mesocarp fibrous; endocarp thick; endsosperm homogeneous. Germination adjacent, viviparous seedling eventually detached from mother plant by elongating plumule.</br></br>One species in Sri Lanka to Ryukyu Islands and Caroline Islands. Introduced and naturalized (invasive?) in West Africa, South America, Central America and the Caribbean.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Creeping tree growing horizontally, and bifurcating at more or less regular intervals. Stem covered by marcescent leaves and persistent leaf bases above ground. Leaves 4–7 in crown, rarely more; sheath and petiole 1.3–1.8 m long; rachis 6–7 m long; pinnae 70–80 per side; the largest ones, the middle of the leaf up to 1.2 m long. Inflorescences 0.9–1.7 m long; peduncle 60–90 cm long, terete; prophyll approximately 30-40 cm long; peduncular bracts 20–30 cm long; rachis 30-80 cm long, rachis bracts tubular; first order branches 5–10; terminal head of female flowers globose, 6–8 cm diam.; male rachillae 7–12 cm long; female flowers with perianth 0.3–0.4 cm long, carpels 0.8–1.1 cm long, stigmatic opening 0.2–0.3 cm long, covered by viscid droplet at anthesis; male flowers much smaller than female flowers, perianth similar in size and shape; common stalk of three stamens 0.4–0.5 cm long. Fruit obovoid, angled, dark brown, 8–11 by 6–8 cm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Tall, clustering, monoecious palms. Individual stems slender, naked and ringed by scars, armed with robust spines below the crown, these usually eroded towards the base on old stems. Leaf sheath tubular forming a well defi ned crownshaft, densely covered by hairs and spines of varying lengths; petiole robust, armed similarly to the sheath in hair covering and armature; blade pinnately divided into numerous, single-fold, regularly arranged, reduplicate, apically acuminate pinnae, lacking spines. Inflorescence protandrous, infrafoliar, erect in bud to pendulous at anthesis, branching to 2 orders; peduncle short; prophyll coriaceous, with dense hair covering, more or less spiny; single peduncular bract similar to prophyll but more sparsely armed; rachis longer than peduncle; first order branches numerous to few, pendulous; rachillae basally with protandrous triads of one central female flower and two lateral male flowers, distally with solitary or paired male flowers. description: Shrubby, creeping to large palms, solitary or clustered, dioecious. Stem with spirally arranged, closely inserted leaf bases. description: Stems clustered, to 2.5 m tall, 1.5 cm diam., dark purplish-brown at the base, green near the crownshaft. Leaves pinnate; sheaths 14–27 cm long, yellowish with brown scales; petioles 10–13 cm long; rachis to 0.7 m long; pinnae 8–13 per side of rachis, usually mottled, somewhat discolorous, linear, regularly arranged, closely spaced, the middle ones 30–35 by 1.3–1.6 cm. Inflorescences pendulous or sometimes erect, spicate or with up to 4 rachillae; peduncles 1–1.8 by 0.2–0.3 cm; rachis, if developed, very short, to 0.5 cm long; rachillae 1–4, 5–20 cm long, straight, circular in cross-section, glabrous; triads arranged distichously, superficial on rachillae. Male flowers not recorded; female flowers c. 0.25 cm long; sepals c. 0.2 by 0.2 cm, rounded, minutely ciliate; petals c. 0.2 by 0.2 cm, minutely ciliate. Fruits ovoid to spindle-shaped, to 1.5 by 1 cm, ripening red to black.

description: Moderate to robust, solitary or clustering, high-climbing, dioecious hapaxanthic rattans. Leaf sheath without knee, usually armed with partial whorls of spines and indumentum; ocrea inconspicuous. Leaf frequently very robust, terminating in a long cirrus; petiole present or absent; leaflets numerous, usually irregularly arranged, grouped and fanned within the groups, often discolorous. Male and female inflorescences superficially similar, produced simultaneously from the topmost nodes; primary axes held ± horizontally, stiff; secondary axes limply pendulous, bearing close imbricate distichous bracts, each one subtending and ± hiding a short branch bearing the flowers. Male flowers with calyx short, terminating in 3 teeth; corolla with 3 petals free almost to the base; stamens 6, shortly epipetalous; pistillode minute; female flower with calyx terminating in 3 lobes; corolla with 3 petals free almost to the base; pistil with fimbriate scaly ovary and 3 stigmas. Fruit 1-seeded, covered in fimbriate or smooth margined scales, the scale tips often reflexed; mesocarp quite thick. Seed with thin sarcotesta; endosperm homogeneous; embryo basal. Seedling leaf lanceolate, undivided; second seedling leaf bifid.</br></br>Sixteen species in E. Himalaya to Hainan and Malesia. Three species in Thailand.

description: Robust, solitary rattan. Stem climbing to 50 m, without sheaths to 6 cm diam. near the base, to 10 cm or more in upper parts, with sheaths to 20 cm diam., internodes to 30 cm long; lower parts of old stems frequently with bulbil-like shoots from the nodes. Leaves cirrate; sheaths dull green, armed with horizontal or oblique combs of golden brown or deep reddish-brown spines to 4 cm long, and abundant white or buff-coloured indumentum; knee absent; petiole to c. 30 cm long; rachis to 4 m long; cirrus to 3 m long; leaflets to c. 60 on each side of the rachis, arranged irregularly in groups of two to seven and fanned within the groups, bluish-green on the upper surface, whitish beneath. Inflorescences produced from the top 7–10 nodes, to c. 80 cm long and bearing c. 12 crowded pendulous branches to c. 1 m; bracts chestnut brown, c. 7 by 5 cm, with triangular tips but scarcely truncate. Male flowers up to c. 20 within each bract; female flowers 3–9 within each bract, ± completely concealed. Mature fruit c. 8 within each bract (if fewer, then fruit larger), very crowded, c. 1.5 cm diam., with reflexed stigmas and covered in c. 50 vertical rows of fimbriate-margined reddish-brown scales. Seed c. 1 cm diam. Seedling leaf lanceolate, undivided.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Robust clustering rattan. Stem climbing to 10 m or more, without sheaths 0.5–4 cm diam., with sheaths 1–10 cm diam., internodes up to c. 30 cm long. Leaves cirrate; leaf sheath mid green, armed with abundant combs of yellow slender spines not exceeding 1.5 cm long, the spines in groups of 20 or more, caducous pale indumentum present on sheath and spines; ocrea absent; knee absent, flagellum absent; petiole very short or absent in distal leaves, to 3 cm long, c. 2 cm wide, deeply channelled; rachis to 3 m long; cirrus to c. 1 m long; leaflets over 40 on each side of the rachis, irregularly arranged in groups and fanned within the groups, the largest 45–50 by 3.5–4 cm, long acuminate in a fine thread to 7 cm long, the lower surface the same colour as the upper surface, never having grey indumentum. Inflorescences produced simultaneously in the axils of many uppermost leaves, the male and female superficially similar, to 2 m long and bearing pendulous first order branches to 80 cm long, bearing conspicuous pale brown bracts, tubular at first, soon splitting along their length, each subtending a short rachilla, bracts in male inflorescences 4–5.5 cm long, male rachillae 2–2.8 cm long, bracts in female inflorescence 4–5.5 cm long, female rachillae 1.2–2.5 cm long, all bracts becoming chestnut brown with age and persisting to fruiting. Fruit at maturity rounded, to 1.5 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.2 by 0.2 cm and covered in c. 26 vertical rows of dull brown scales with smooth margins and non-spiny tips. Seed rounded, basally somewhat flattened, c. 0.9 cm diam.; endosperm homogeneous.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Moderately robust, clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 35 m long, without sheaths 0.5–4 cm diam., with sheaths 1–9 cm diam., internodes up to c. 30 cm long, the stem generally very slender near the ground, much more robust distally, particularly just before flowering. Leaves cirrate; sheaths mid green, armed with scattered, golden, needle-like spines, 1–2 cm long, sometimes arranged in horizontal combs of no more than 5 spines, abundant caducous dark indumentum, spines shorter, sparser on distal sheaths; ocrea absent; knee absent; flagellum absent; petiole in distal leaves very short or absent, not exceeding c. 3 by up to 2.5 cm; rachis to 3 m long; cirrus to 1 m long; leaflets up to 40 on each side of the rachis, irregularly arranged in groups and fanned within the groups, the largest 40–55 by 3.5–4 cm, adaxially shiny dark green, abaxially with a fugacious layer of white indumentum, usually conspicuous on newly emerged leaves, sometimes long persistent, the leaflets generally lacking bristles. Inflorescences male and female superficially similar, produced simultaneously from many topmost nodes (up to 15 or more) the basalmost to 1.5 m long, decreasing in length towards the stem tip, the longest with up to 15 pendulous first order branches; first order branches bearing conspicuous pale yellowish-green, reddish-brown tipped bracts, tubular at first, soon splitting along their length, each subtending a short rachilla, bracts in male inflorescences 1.9–4 cm long, male rachillae 0.8–1.9 cm long, bracts in female inflorescence 2.5–4 cm long, female rachillae 1.2–2 cm long, all bracts becoming chestnut brown with age and persisting to fruiting. Fruit at maturity rounded, to 2 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.2 by 0.2 cm and covered in c. 35 vertical rows of dull brown scales with smooth margins and non-spiny tips. Seed rounded, basally somewhat flattened, c. 1.2 cm diam.; endosperm homogeneous.

description: Clustering high-climbing dioecious hapaxanthic rattans with moderate to robust stems. Leaf cirrate, sheaths without knees, ocrea sometimes conspicuous; rachis bearing entire ± regularly arranged concolorous leaflets. Inflorescences produced simultaneously in the axils of the uppermost leaves, male and female superficially similar; primary axis branching to 1 or 2 orders, the branches bearing tubular triangular-tipped bracts subtending clusters of 2–7 flowers. Male flower with tubular calyx with 3 triangular lobes and 3 petals joined at the base; stamens 6, borne on the petals; pistillode minute; female flower with tubular calyx with 3 very short obtuse lobes, and corolla with 3 lobes; staminodes 6 epipetalous; ovary tipped with 3 small divergent stigmas; calyx enlarging considerably and splitting irregularly, persisting to mature fruiting; corolla also persistent. Mature fruit tipped with minute stigmatic remains, covered in many somewhat irregular vertical rows of scales. Seed with thin sarcotesta; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf bifid.</br></br>Six or seven species known from Myanmar and Thailand south to Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra, Billiton and Borneo. Two species in Thailand. A genus of rather coarse clustering rattans normally found in secondary forest or seral facies of primary forest (such as old landslips or the clearings formed by the death or fall of large trees). Generally not used as the cane has a soft pith and poor external appearance. However, the apex of at least one species is eaten in some parts of Borneo.

description: Clustering, moderate to robust rattan, forming rather dense thickets. Stems to 30 m or more, without sheaths to 3 cm diam., with sheaths to 6 cm diam., but usually more slender, internodes to 40 cm, shorter in exposed stems. Leaves cirrate; sheaths generally dull green with persistent grey tomentum and scattered caducous reddish-brown scales, and abundant scattered golden-yellow spines to 0.8 cm long, the spines sometimes absent on the sheaths subtending the inflorescences; ocrea irregular, oblique, fibrous and tattering; petiole absent in adult stems; rachis to 2 m long; cirrus to 1 m; leaflets c. 30 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, the largest to 40 by 4 cm, bright shining green, concolorous, with short bristles along the margins, the mid nerve on the upper surface usually with conspicuous golden bristles to 1.5 cm. Inflorescences up to 15 produced simultaneously, the male with more slender branches than the female, to 40 cm, with curving branches to 30 cm bearing clusters of flowers. Ripe fruit oblate, to 2.5 by 3 cm, covered in up to 42 vertical rows of pale greenish to chestnut brown scales. Seed c. 2 by 2 cm; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf bifid.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Clustering, moderate-sized rattan forming rather dense thickets. Stems climbing to 30 m long, without sheaths distinctly triangular in cross section, to 1.3 cm diam., with sheaths to 2 cm diam., internodes to 40 cm near the ground, usually much less (c. 20 cm) in stems in the forest canopy. Leaves cirrate; sheaths dull green, armed with evenly scattered, slightly upward pointing golden spines to 0.3 cm long and covered with sparse reddish-brown indumentum; ocrea very short, to 0.5 cm long, truncate, golden brown; flagellum absent; petiole to c. 15 cm long, densely covered in caducous red brown scales and abaxially very sparsely armed with reflexed spines; rachis to 90 cm long; cirrus to c. 1 m long; leaflets 15–20 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, rather distant (c. 5 cm apart), the longest to c. 30 by 3 cm, acuminate in long drip tips, armed along the adaxial surface of the main vein with short golden spinules to 0.2 cm long. Inflorescences to 30 cm long, produced simultaneously from the axils of the uppermost reduced leaves, the male branched to 2 orders, the female to 1 order; first order branches to c. 20 cm long. Male flowers borne on very short c. 0.8 cm, strongly curved branches from bracts on the first order branches; female flowers borne in groups of 2 or 3 flowers only. Mature fruit borne on persistent enlarged and split calyx and corolla, slightly oblate and obscurely three-angled, c. 2.5 by 3 cm, with a short beak to 1 by 1 mm, and covered in c. 22 vertical rows of yellow brown scales with dark margins. Seed c. 2 by 1.5 cm; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf unknown.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Small, clustering palm, dioecious or polygamous. Stem slender, bamboo-like, erect, covered by persistent leaf bases, eventually naked and conspicuously ringed by leaf scars. Leaf palmate, induplicate; sheath dissolving into loose mesh of interlocking fibres; petiole elongate, slender, unarmed; adaxial hastula small, abaxial one absent; blade circular in outline, entire to deeply bifid, splitting in single- to several-folded, apically toothed segments, tranverse veinlets conspicuous. Inflorescence interfoliar, branching to 1–3 orders; peduncle short, often contained in leaf sheath; prophyll splitting longitudinally on abaxial face; peduncular bract lacking; rachis longer than peduncle, with tubular rachis bracts, the proximal 1–2 conspicuously enlarged; rachillae spreading to crowded in male inflorescences, with spirally arranged, solitary, rarely paired flowers. Male and female flowers similar in overall shape, size and in the perianth parts; sepals fused in shallow cup-shaped calyx; petals much longer than calyx, connate into fleshy corolla tube, further elongated especially in the male flowers by stalk-like extension of the receptacle above the calyx; stamens six, adnate basally to corolla tube, with short anthers, staminodes when present reduced in size; gynoecium of three free carpels, glabrous, apically with minute tube-shaped stigma. Fruit usually developing from one carpel only, globose, purplish brown to white at maturity; epicarp smooth; mesocarp fleshy; endocarp thin. Seed with homogeneous endosperm and lateral intrusion of seed coat. Germination remote-tubular.</br></br>Eight species in S China to Indo-China. Two species in Thailand.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Loosely clustered, shrubby to moderate-sized palm. Individual stems 1–2(–3) m, 0.8–1.5 cm diam. (without leaf sheath remnants), often rhizomatous basally. Leaves 8–20 in crown; leaf sheath 5–12 cm long; petiole 15–30 cm long, 0.3–0.5 cm across; blade ½–4/5-circular in outline, flattened to open funnel-shaped, darker and more glossy green above, up to 50 cm diam., evenly split to 1–9 cm from hastula, in 5–12, 15–27-folded segments. Male and female inflorescences similar, branched to 2 orders, to 25–35 cm long, basalmost rachis bract conspicuously inflated, rachis 5–10(–15) cm long with two first order branches, rachillae 5–15, 1.5–6(–10) cm long. Flowers 0.3–0.4 cm long, different sexual types of flowers similar, calyx regularly lobed, often with striate pigmentation, male and hermaphrodite flowers clearly longer than the female ones. Fruit ellipsoid to ovoid, 0.8–1.2 cm diam., borne on an c. 0.5 mm long receptacular stalk.

description: Tightly clustered, small-sized palm forming large clumps. Individual stems 2–3 m tall, 0.4–1.5 cm diam. (without leaf sheath remnants). Leaves 7–18 in crown; leaf sheath 10–15 cm long, often with persistent ligule; petiole 20–25 cm long, 0.15–0.2 cm across; blade ½–4/5-circular in outline, flattened, pale green abaxially as well as adaxially, variable in size up to 40 cm diam., splitting variable to 0.1–17 cm from hastula, segments 2–11, 7–25-folded. Male and female inflorescence similar, branched to 1–2 orders, to 30–50(–60) cm long, prophyll and rachis bracts similar, overlapping not inflated; rachis 6–30 cm long with two first order branches, rachillae usually few, 3–25 cm long. Flowers 0.5–0.65 cm long, different sexual types of flowers similar, calyx irregularly lobed, evenly pigmented, male flowers slightly longer than the female and hermaphrodite ones. Fruit globose, 0.8–1 cm diam., borne on an up to 0.2 cm long receptacular stalk.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Moderate-sized clustering, pleonanthic or hapaxanthic dioecious palms. Stem subterranean, decumbent or shortly erect, internodes short, usually obscured by the persistent leaf bases. Leaves pinnate; leaf sheath and petiole elongate, open, not forming a crownshaft, armed with flattened spines, arranged in rows or whorls; leaflet single-fold, except for the terminal pair which is usually joined, linear or sigmoid in outline, equally spaced and orientated in one plane or grouped and pointing in different directions, acuminate. Inflorescence axillary and emerging though a groove along the abaxial surface of the leaf base or inflorescences terminal and subtended by reduced leaves, sometimes spicate, male inflorescences usually branched to 1 more order than female; peduncle short; prophyll rather inconspicuous, partly enclosed within the leaf sheath slit. Male flowers borne in dyads, sunken in pits, exserted at anthesis; calyx tubular, 3-lobed; corolla often with a short stalk-like base, and a long proximal tube, bearing 3 triangular, valvate lobes; stamens 6, borne at the mouth of corolla tube, filament short, anthers rounded to elongate. Female flowers either solitary or coupled with a sterile male flower in dyads, gynoecium tricarpellate, triovulate, covered with flattened scales, stigmas 3. Fruit (1–)3-seeded, globose to pear-shaped or ellipsoidal, with apical stigmatic remains; epicarp covered in somewhat irregular vertical rows of reflexed scales, the scale tips spinelike and upward pointing, mesocarp thin at maturity, endocarp not differentiated. Seed with thick sarcotesta, endosperm homogeneous, the apex with a pit. Germination adjacent ligular; eophyll entire, bifid.</br></br>Twenty species in India (Assam) to S China and W Malesia. Four species in Thailand.

description: Densely clustered understorey palm up to 7 m tall. Stem erect or creeping, to 1 m tall, 5–12 m diam. Leaves 9–18 per stem; sheath 45–60 cm long, deeply split, densely covered with brownish indument and armed with more or less complete whorls of 1–5 cm long, yellow to distally black spines; petiole 2–3 m long, greenish-yellow, otherwise as sheath; rachis 2–4 m long; leaflets 23–30 per side, clustered in groups of 3–4 and pointing in different directions to regularly arranged in one plane toward the apex, sigmoid, 45–60 by 5 cm, acuminate, apical leaflets coherent. Inflorescences 2–4 per stem, lateral, emerging though groove on the abaxial side of the leaf base; male inflorescence 30–60 cm long with 10–25 branches, partial inflorescences spike-like, 8–12 cm long, glabrous; female inflorescence to 25 cm long with fewer branches, partial spike-like inflorescence 5–12 cm long. Fruit c. 4.5 by 3 cm, pear-shaped or obovoid, beaked, densely covered with reddish, spine-like scales.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Salacca glabrescens . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 486. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Acaulescent caespitose palm, stems short and subterranean. Leaves 10–15 per stem; sheath and petiole not distinct from each other, to 2.9 m long, densely covered with spines in groups of 2–10; rachis to 4.5 m long; leafl ets 35–42 per side, evenly spaced and arranged in one plane, lanceolate, 83–125 by 4–7 cm, above with small spines along the major veins, apical pair of leaflets usually split. Inflorescences several per stem, terminal, erect, compact, branched to second order, subtended by much reduced leaves and covered with overlapping bracts, subtending bracts of floral dyads and individual flowers tomentose to densely hairy on the abaxial surface; male inflorescence to 100 cm long, with spike-like 13–24 cm long partial inflorescences; female inflorescence 30–40 cm long, with 7–10, 8–12 cm long spike-like partial inflorescences, inserted more or less distichously. Fruit 5–6 by 6–8 cm, obovoid beaked, densely covered with reddish, spine-like scales.

description: Loosly clustering understorey palm, up to 4 m tall. Stems creeping to shortly erect, with conspicuous aerial roots. Leaves 6–9 per stem; sheath 30–60 cm long, deeply split, densely covered with brownish, felt-like indument and armed with up to 4 cm long slender black spines, arranged in horizontal groups of 3–7 basally to paired or solitary towards the petiole; petiole c. 1.2 m long; rachis 2–2.5 m long, armed abaxially with solitary or paired spines to 1.5 cm long; leaflets 15–17 per side, clustered in subopposite groups of 2–3 and pointing in different directions, sigmoid, c. 50 by 5 cm, long acuminate, apical pair of leaflets coherent, not split. Male inflorescence lateral, emerging though groove on the abaxial side of the leaf base, to 4 m long, whip-like, with c. 3 partial inflorescences, these reddish, spike-like and up to 20 cm long, with hairs projecting from the subtending bracts; female inflorescences not seen. Fruits ellipsoid to obovoid, densely covered in spine-like scales.

description: Large clustering palm, up to 12 m tall. Stem creeping to 5 m long and 20 cm diam., with many adventitious roots. Leaves 12–18 per stem; sheath to 1 m long; petiole 5–7.5 m long, sheath and petiole heavily armed with more or less complete whorls of up to 8 cm long, black spines; rachis 5–7 m long; leaflets 40–60 per side, clustered in groups of 2–5 and pointing in different directions, sigmoid, 0.7–1 by c. 0.08 m, acuminate, apical pair of leaflets coherent, not split and wide. Inflorescences 2–3 per stem, lateral, emerging though groove on the abaxial side of the leaf base; male inflorescence 2–3 m long, pendulous often lying on the ground, with 10 first order branches, each bearing 10 spike-like, reddish, up to 10 cm long, hairy rachillae; female inflorescences up to 0.7 m long, with fewer branches, each bearing spike-like rachillae similar to those of the male inflorescence. Fruits 7–8 by 4–5 cm, obovoid, densely covered with reddish-brown spine-like scales.

description: Shrubby to moderate-sized, solitary or clustering palms, dioecious or polygamous. Stem decumbent or erect, distally covered by skirt of dead leaves and persistant leaf bases. Leaf palmate, induplicate; sheath dissolving into mesh of fine and course fibres; petiole elongate, unarmed or rarely with very fine teeth; adaxial hastula well developed, abaxial one absent; blade almost circular, glaucous green abaxially in several species, splitting equally to unequally along adaxial ribs into numerous, single-fold segments, these shallowly indented at the tip. Inflorescence interfoliar; branching to 4 orders; peduncle short; prophyll conspicuous, with caducous tomentum; peduncular bracts 1–3; rachis shorter or longer than peduncle; rachis bracts tubular basally. Male and female flowers similar in overall size, shape and in the perianth parts; sepals united at the base; petals free, much longer than the calyx; stamens 6, filaments free, with short anthers, staminodes when present similar but with empty anthers; gynoecium of three, free carpels, hairy, apically with partially open, stigmatic slits. Fruit usually developing from one carpel only, kidney-shaped to oblong, purplish-black at maturity; epicarp hairy in young fruits to glabrous at maturity; mesocarp thin; endocarp crustaceous. Seed with homogeneous endosperm, with lateral intrusion of the seed coat. Germination remote-tubular.</br></br>Eight species in Himalaya to S China. One species in Thailand.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Trachycarpus  . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 3, 2013. Pg. 490. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Solitary polygamo-dioecious palm. Stem up to 9 m tall at maturity, 10–16 cm diam., erect, naked, conspicuously ringed. Leaves 20–25 in crown; sheath c. 25–30 cm long dissolving in spreading fine fibres; petiole 40–50 cm long, margins minutely toothed and somewhat tomentose; adaxial hastula prominent to 3 cm long; blade rounded in outline, moderately undulate to flat, 0.9–1.1 m diam., evenly splitting to c. ½ radius into 60–90, single-folded segments, individual segments shortly indented, green adaxially, glaucous green abaxially. Inflorescences 3–5 on one palm, arching, prophyll 15–25 cm long, peduncular bracts and rachis bracts similar, 15–35 cm long, decreasing in length towards the distal parts, tubular proximally, inflated distally; male inflorescences 30–50 cm long, with 15–20 cm long peduncle; female (sometimes hermaphrodite?) inflorescences 0.8–1 m long, with 30–50 cm long peduncle; rachillae 3–10 cm long, stiff. Flowers minute in bud. Fruit kidney-shaped, 0.6–0.8 cm long and 10–12 cm wide, yellow to yellowish-brown at maturity.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Small monoecious, understorey palms to small trees. Stems clustered, rarely solitary. Leaves usually few in crown, separated by long internodes, spirally or distichously arranged, leaf sheath elongate, ligulate, disintegrating in fibrous mesh, petiole rounded in cross section, pinnae induplicate, lanceolate, entire to irregularly lobed, praemorse, leaf apex composed of several unsplit pinnae. Inflorescence spicate or branched to one order, peduncular bracts numerous, chartaceous, brown tomentose, male inflorescences lateral, flower clusters spirally arranged, composed of two male flowers flanking an aborted female flower, petals free, stamens 3–19, pistillode absent; female inflorescence terminal, with spirally arranged solitary flowers, petals fused into three-lobed corolla, staminodes absent. Fruit ovoid to oblong, with apical stigmatic residue.</br></br>Eight species in Himalaya to S China. Three species in Thailand.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Caespitose shrub with individual stems up to 3 m tall, 2–10 cm diam. Leaves 4–7, spirally arranged; petiole 0.8–1.5 m long; rachis 0.9–1.5 m long, with 8–12 pinnae per side, alternate, more or less evenly spaced except basally, and distributed in one plane, longest ones in the middle, up to 50 cm long, lanceolate, with two conspicuous lobes. Male inflorescence 40–50 cm long, with up to 30 cm long peduncle, branched to the first order with c. 25, up to 21 cm long rachillae, male flowers 0.5–0.6 cm long, yellow, stamens 11–16; female inflorescence 40–50 cm long, with up to 25 cm long peduncle, branched to first order, with 7–17, up to 20 cm long rachillae, female flowers up to 0.25 cm long. Fruit ellipsoid, up to 1.7 by 0.8 cm, red.

description: Solitary palm tree up to 6 m tall. Stem 15–25 cm diam. Leaves arranged more or less distichously; sheath 40–60 cm long, disintegrating into an outer layer of coarse fibres interlocking with an inner layer of finer fibres; petiole 0.5–1.5 m long; rachis 1.8–3.5 m long, with 43–73 pinnae, these irregularly arranged in groups of 3–8 pointing in different directions, longest ones in the middle, up to 80 cm long, linear to lanceolate, shallowly lobed. Male inflorescences to 1.2 m long, with up to 0.5 m long peduncle, branched to the first order with c. 1000, up to 30 cm long rachillae, flowers up to 1 cm long, beige with purplish tinge, stamens 8–15; female inflorescence to 1 m long, peduncle to 50 cm long, with 40–50, up to 60 cm long rachillae, female flowers 0.2 cm long. Fruit ovoid to ellipsoid, up to 2.2 by 1.5 cm, reddish-brown.

description: Caespitose shrub with individual stems up to 1.6 m tall and 4–10 cm diam. Leaves spirally arranged; sheath 30–75 cm long; petiole 1–1.5 m long; rachis 0.8–1.3 m long, with 5–10 pinnae per side, alternate, more or less evenly spaced except basally, and distributed in one plane, longest ones in the middle, up to 80 cm long, lanceolate, not lobed or indistinctly so. Male inflorescences to 10, up to 20 cm long rachillae, flowers up to 0.6 cm long, stamens 16–19; female inflorescences with rachillae up to 11 cm long, female flowers c. 0.3 cm long. Fruit ovoid, up to 11 by 8 mm, red to purple.
